title.zh: 卷四十八 列傳第三十八 陸澄 陸慧曉 陸杲
title.en: Volume 48 Biographies 38: Lu Cheng, Lu Huxiao, Lu Gao
title.raw: 卷四十八 列傳第三十八 陸澄 陸慧曉 陸杲 Volume 48 Biographies 38: Lu Cheng, Lu Huxiao, Lu Gao

sentences.zh: 澄少好學，博覽無所不知，行坐眠食，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: From youth Cheng loved learning; he read widely and knew everything. Whether walking, sitting, sleeping, or eating, he never let a scroll leave his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng loved study from boyhood and read so widely that he seemed to know everything. Whether he was walking, sitting, asleep, or at table, he never put his books down.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，為尚書殿中郎，議皇后諱班下應依舊稱姓。

translations.literal: In the early Taishi era of Song he served as Secretariat Acting Registrar and argued that in taboo lists for the empress her surname should still be used according to former practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taishi reign of Song he was made acting registrar in the Secretariat and argued that taboo lists for the empress should continue to give her surname as before.

sentences.zh: 左丞徐爰案司馬孚議皇后不稱姓，春秋逆王后于齊，並不言姓。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Xu Yuan cited Sima Fu's view that an empress should not be called by surname, noting that when the Spring and Autumn Annals records the queen going to Qi it never gives her surname.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Xu Yuan invoked Sima Fu's argument that an empress should not be named by surname, pointing out that when the Spring and Autumn Annals records the queen's journey to Qi, it never mentions her surname.

sentences.zh: 澄以意立議，坐免官，白衣領職。

translations.literal: Cheng advanced his own opinion and was dismissed from office for it, though he continued his duties in plain dress without official rank.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng pressed his own view and was stripped of office for it, though he kept performing his duties in plain dress without rank.

sentences.zh: 郎官舊坐杖，有名無實，澄在官積前後罰凡至千數。

translations.literal: Beating was nominally prescribed for Secretariat officers but rarely enforced; during his tenure Cheng actually imposed such penalties hundreds and even thousands of times.
translations.idiomatic: Corporal punishment was nominally prescribed for secretariat officers but almost never applied; Cheng, in office, actually ordered beatings hundreds and even thousands of times.

sentences.zh: 後兼左丞。

translations.literal: He later also served concurrently as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He later held the Left Vice Director post as well.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，詔皇太子朝服袞冕九章，澄與儀曹郎丘仲起議：「服冕以朝，實著經文，秦除六冕，漢明還備。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi an edict ordered the crown prince to wear court dress with dragon robe and nine emblems. Cheng and Qiu Zhongqi of the Protocol Office memorialized: "Wearing the dragon robe at court is clearly established in canonical texts; Qin abolished the six caps, and Emperor Ming of Han restored them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi the crown prince was ordered to wear court dress with dragon robe and nine emblems. Cheng and Qiu Zhongqi of the protocol office argued: "Wearing the dragon robe at court is plainly set out in the classics; Qin abolished the six caps, and Emperor Ming of Han restored them.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，不欲令臣下服袞冕，故位公者加侍官。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin they did not wish subordinates to wear dragon robes, so those of ducal rank were given attendant offices instead.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Jin, rulers had not wanted subjects to wear dragon robes, so men of ducal rank were given attendant offices instead.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子禮絕群後，宜遵聖王盛典，革近代之制。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince's ritual surpasses all others; he should follow the sage-kings' grand ceremonies and reform recent custom.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's ritual standing now surpasses everyone else's; he should follow the great ceremonies of the sage-kings and set aside recent practice.

sentences.zh: 」累遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: " He was promoted in due course to Inspectorate Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose in due course to censor-in-chief of the inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 儉答曰：「易體微遠，實貫群籍，豈可專據小王便為該備，依舊存鄭，高同來說。

translations.literal: Jian replied: "The Changes is subtle and far-reaching and truly runs through all the classics; how can we rely on Wang Bi's commentary alone as sufficient? Keep Zheng Xuan's as before and rank it with the later schools.
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered: "The Changes is subtle and far-reaching and truly underlies all the classics; we cannot treat Wang Bi's commentary alone as sufficient. Keep Zheng Xuan's as before and give it equal standing with the later schools.

sentences.zh: 元凱注傳，超邁前儒，谷梁小書，無俟兩注。

translations.literal: Du Yu's commentary and tradition surpass the earlier Confucians; the Guliang is a minor classic and needs no second commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu's commentary and tradition outstrip the earlier Confucians; the Guliang is a minor classic and needs no second commentary.

sentences.zh: 存麋略範，率由舊式。

translations.literal: Keep the Mao school's Brief Exemplar and follow the old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the Mao school's Brief Exemplar and adhere to the established form.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸議，並同雅論。

translations.literal: All these proposals agree with the refined opinion.
translations.idiomatic: On all these points I agree with your refined view.

sentences.zh: 疑孝經非鄭所注，僕以此書明百行之首，實人倫所先，七略、藝文並陳之六藝，不與蒼頡、凡將之流也。

translations.literal: I doubt whether the Classic of Filial Piety was annotated by Zheng Xuan. I hold that this book illuminates the head of the hundred practices and truly comes first in human relations; both the Qilue and the Yiwen list it among the Six Classics, not with works like the Cangjie or Fanjiang primers.
translations.idiomatic: I doubt that the Classic of Filial Piety was annotated by Zheng Xuan. I take this book to illuminate the foremost of the hundred practices and to stand first in human relations; both the Qilue and the Yiwen place it among the Six Classics, not with primers such as the Cangjie or Fanjiang.

sentences.zh: 鄭注虛實，前代不嫌，意謂可安，仍舊立置。」

translations.literal: Whether Zheng's commentary is authentic or not, previous ages did not object; I think it can stand and should remain in place as before."
translations.idiomatic: Whether Zheng's commentary is genuine is disputed, but earlier ages did not mind; I believe it can rest undisturbed and should remain established as before."

sentences.zh: 儉自以博聞多識，讀書過澄。

translations.literal: Jian considered himself widely learned and thought he had read more than Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jian took himself for erudite and believed he had read more than Cheng.

sentences.zh: 澄謂曰：「僕少來無事，唯以讀書為業；

translations.literal: Cheng said to him: "I have had nothing to do since youth except make reading my occupation;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng told him: "Since youth I have had nothing to do but read;

sentences.zh: 且年位已高。

translations.literal: and my years and rank are already advanced.
translations.idiomatic: and my years and rank are already advanced.

sentences.zh: 令君少便鞅掌王務，雖復一覽便諳，然見卷軸未必多僕。

translations.literal: You have handled state affairs since youth; though you grasp things at a glance, I wonder whether you have seen as many scrolls as I have.
translations.idiomatic: You have managed state affairs since you were young; though you grasp things at a glance, I doubt you have seen as many scrolls as I have.

sentences.zh: 」儉集學士何憲等盛自商略，澄待儉語畢，然後談所遺漏數百十條，皆儉所未睹。

translations.literal: " Jian gathered the academicians He Xian and others and discussed at length. Cheng waited until Jian had finished, then spoke of several hundred points Jian had overlooked, all of which Jian had never seen.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian gathered the academicians He Xian and others and held forth at length. Cheng waited until he had finished, then raised several hundred omissions Jian had never noticed.

sentences.zh: 儉乃嘆服。

translations.literal: Jian sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Jian could only sigh in admiration.

sentences.zh: 儉在尚書省出巾箱几案雜服飾，令學士隸事事多者與之，人人各得一兩物。

translations.literal: At the Secretariat Jian produced scarf-boxes, desk items, and assorted ornaments and had the academicians identify the most items; each man received one or two.
translations.idiomatic: At the Secretariat Jian brought out scarf-boxes, desk pieces, and assorted ornaments and had the academicians name as many as they could; each man took away one or two.

sentences.zh: 澄後來，更出諸人所不知事，復各數條，並舊物奪將去。

translations.literal: Cheng came later, produced more things no one else knew, several items each, and took back the earlier objects as well.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng arrived afterward, named several more items no one else knew, and took back the things the others had already claimed.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍，秘書監，吳郡中正，光祿大夫，加給事中，尋領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat Library, Rectifier for Wu Commandery, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with additional appointment as Palace Attendant, and soon after headed the Imperial University as Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He became regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, director of the secretariat library, rectifier for Wu commandery, and grand master for splendid happiness, with an additional appointment as palace attendant, and soon headed the imperial university as libationer.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良得古器，小口方腹，而底平可容七八升，以問澄。

translations.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling obtained an ancient vessel with a narrow mouth and square belly, flat bottom holding seven or eight sheng, and asked Cheng about it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling acquired an ancient vessel with a narrow mouth, square belly, and flat base holding seven or eight sheng, and asked Cheng what it was.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「此名服匿，單于以與蘇武。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "This is called a fu-ni; the Chanyu gave one to Su Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said: "This is called a fu-ni; the Chanyu gave one to Su Wu.

sentences.zh: 」子良詳視器底有字，彷佛可識，如澄所言。

translations.literal: " Ziliang examined the bottom closely and found characters faintly legible, just as Cheng had said.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziliang looked closely at the base and found characters faintly legible, exactly as Cheng had said.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，以老疾，轉光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，未拜，卒，諡靜子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, on account of age and illness, he was transferred to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with additional appointment as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; before he could take up the post he died, posthumous name Jingzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang, owing to age and illness, he was made grand master for splendid happiness with an additional appointment as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry; before he could assume office he died, and was given the posthumous name Jingzi.

sentences.zh: 澄當世稱為碩學，讀易三年不解文義，欲撰宋書竟不成。

translations.literal: Cheng was acclaimed in his age as a great scholar, yet read the Changes for three years without grasping its meaning and wished to compile a History of Song but never finished it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was hailed in his day as a great scholar, yet read the Changes for three years without understanding it and tried to write a history of Song but never finished.

sentences.zh: 王儉戲之曰：「陸公，書廚也。

translations.literal: Wang Jian joked: "Master Lu is a book cupboard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian teased him: "Master Lu is a walking bookcase.

sentences.zh: 」家多墳籍，人所罕見，撰地理書及雜傳，死後乃出。

translations.literal: " His household held many rare tomes seldom seen by others; he wrote a geographical work and miscellaneous biographies that appeared only after his death.
translations.idiomatic: " His house held many rare books others seldom saw; he wrote a geographical work and miscellaneous biographies that appeared only after his death.

sentences.zh: 澄弟鮮，得罪宋世，當死。

translations.literal: Cheng's younger brother Xian offended the Song court and was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's younger brother Xian had offended the Song court and was condemned to die.

sentences.zh: 澄于路見舍人王道隆叩頭流血，以此見原。

translations.literal: On the road Cheng saw Palace Attendant Wang Daolong and knocked his head until it bled; through this Xian was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Cheng met palace attendant Wang Daolong and knocked his head until it bled; by this Xian was spared.

sentences.zh: 揚州主簿顧測以兩奴就鮮質錢，鮮死，子暉誣為買券。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Registrar Gu Ce had pledged two slaves to Xian for a loan; after Xian died, his son Hui falsely claimed they had been sold outright.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou registrar Gu Ce had pledged two slaves to Xian as security for a loan; after Xian died, his son Hui falsely claimed they had been sold outright.

sentences.zh: 澄為中丞，測遂為澄所抑，世以此少之。

translations.literal: When Cheng became Censor-in-Chief, Ce was suppressed by him, and the age thought somewhat less of Cheng for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng became censor-in-chief, Ce was thwarted by him, and contemporaries thought somewhat less of Cheng for it.

sentences.zh: 陸慧曉

translations.literal: Lu Huxiao
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huxiao

sentences.zh: 陸慧曉字叔明，吳郡吳人，晉太尉玩之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Huxiao, style name Shuming, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery, great-great-grandson of Jin Grand Commandant Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huxiao, style Shuming, was from Wu in Wu commandery, the great-great-grandson of Jin grand commandant Wan.

sentences.zh: 自玩至慧曉祖萬載，世為侍中，皆有名行。

translations.literal: From Wan down to Huxiao's grandfather Wanzai, the family for generations held the post of Palace Attendant, all men of reputation and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From Wan down to Huxiao's grandfather Wanzai, the family had held the palace attendant post for generations, each man noted for character and conduct.

sentences.zh: 慧曉伯父仲元，又為侍中，時人方之金、張二族。

translations.literal: Huxiao's uncle Zhongyuan also served as Palace Attendant; contemporaries ranked the family with the clans of Jin and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Huxiao's uncle Zhongyuan also served as palace attendant; people of the day ranked the Lu with the Jin and Zhang clans.

sentences.zh: 父子真，仕宋為海陵太守。

translations.literal: His father Zizhen served Song as Governor of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zizhen served Song as governor of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人秋當見幸，家在海陵，假還葬父，子真不與相聞。

translations.literal: At the time Secretariat Attendant Qiu Dang enjoyed imperial favor; his family was in Hailing, and he took leave to bury his father, but Zizhen would not communicate with him.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat attendant Qiu Dang was then in favor; his family was in Hailing, and he took leave to bury his father, but Zizhen would not deal with him.

sentences.zh: 當請發人修橋，又以妨農不許。

translations.literal: Dang requested laborers to repair a bridge, but Zizhen refused on the ground that it would hinder farming.
translations.idiomatic: Dang asked for laborers to repair a bridge, but Zizhen refused on the ground that it would interfere with the harvest.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康聞而賞之。

translations.literal: Prince Pengcheng Yikang heard of it and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pengcheng Yikang heard of it and praised him.

sentences.zh: 王僧達貴公子孫，以才傲物，為吳郡太守，入昌門曰：「彼有人焉。

translations.literal: Wang Sengda, a nobleman's son, was proud of his talent and looked down on others. As Governor of Wu Commandery he entered Chang Gate and said: "There are men of note over there.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda, a nobleman's son, was gifted and arrogant. As governor of Wu commandery he entered Chang Gate and said: "There are men of note over there.

sentences.zh: 顧琛一公兩掾，英英門戶；

translations.literal: Gu Chen is one duke and two aides—a splendid household;
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen is one duke and two aides—a splendid house;

sentences.zh: 陸子真五世內侍，我之流亞。

translations.literal: Lu Zizhen has five generations of inner attendants—my own rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zizhen has five generations of inner attendants—men of my own rank.

sentences.zh: 」子真自臨海太守眼疾歸，為中散大夫，卒。

translations.literal: " Zizhen returned from his post as Governor of Linhai because of eye trouble, was made Master of the Palace for Scattered Cavalry, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Zizhen came back from Linhai because of eye trouble, was made master of the palace for scattered cavalry, and died.

sentences.zh: 慧曉清介正立，不雜交遊，同郡張緒稱之曰：「江東裴、樂也。

translations.literal: Huxiao was upright and austere, mingled little in society, and Zhang Xu of the same commandery called him "the Pei and Yue of the lower Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Huxiao was upright and austere and kept to himself; Zhang Xu of the same commandery called him "the Pei and Yue of the lower Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 」初應州郡辟，舉秀才，曆諸府行參軍，以母老還家侍養，十餘年不仕。

translations.literal: " At first he answered provincial and commandery summons, was nominated as a cultivated talent, and served as traveling aide in several offices; when his mother grew old he went home to care for her and did not take office for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: " He first answered provincial summons, was nominated cultivated talent, and served as traveling aide in several offices; when his mother grew old he went home to care for her and held no office for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝輔政，除為尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi was regent, Huxiao was appointed Secretariat Acting Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi was regent, Huxiao was made acting registrar in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鄰族來相賀，慧曉舉酒曰：「陸慧曉年踰三十，婦父領選，始作尚書郎，卿輩乃復以為慶邪？」

translations.literal: Neighbors came to congratulate him. Huxiao raised his cup and said: "Lu Huxiao is past thirty; his father-in-law heads the selection office, and he is only now made a Secretariat officer—do you really take this for a celebration?"
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors came to congratulate him. Huxiao raised his cup and said: "Lu Huxiao is past thirty; his father-in-law runs personnel selection, and I am only now made a secretariat officer—do you really mean to celebrate this?"

sentences.zh: 高帝表禁奢侈，慧曉撰答詔草，為帝所賞，引為太傅東合祭酒。

translations.literal: The Emperor memorialized to forbid extravagance; Huxiao drafted the reply edict and was commended by the throne, then summoned as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor memorialized to forbid extravagance; Huxiao drafted the reply edict, won the throne's praise, and was made libationer of the grand tutor's eastern pavilion.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，遷太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan of Qi he was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jianyuan he was made groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 廬江何點常稱「慧曉心如照鏡，遇形觸物，無不朗然。

translations.literal: He Dian of Lujiang often said: "Huxiao's mind is like a bright mirror; whatever form or thing it meets, nothing fails to appear clear.
translations.idiomatic: He Dian of Lujiang often said: "Huxiao's mind is like a bright mirror; whatever he meets, nothing stays obscure.

sentences.zh: 王思遠恒如懷冰，暑月亦有霜氣」。

translations.literal: Wang Siyuan is always as if holding ice—even in midsummer there is a frost about him."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Siyuan is always as if holding ice—even in midsummer he seems frosted."

sentences.zh: 當時以為實錄。

translations.literal: People of the time took this as an accurate record.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day took this for the plain truth.

sentences.zh: 慧曉與張融並宅，其間有池，池上有二株楊柳。

translations.literal: Huxiao and Zhang Rong lived on adjoining estates; between them was a pond with two willows above it.
translations.idiomatic: Huxiao and Zhang Rong lived on adjoining estates with a pond between them and two willows above the water.

sentences.zh: 點歎曰：「此池便是醴泉，此木便是交讓。

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "This pond is the Sweet Spring itself; these trees are the Hand-over Trees.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said: "This pond is the Sweet Spring itself; these trees are the Hand-over Trees.

sentences.zh: 」及武陵王曄守會稽，上為精選僚吏，以慧曉為征虜功曹，與府參軍沛國劉璡同從述職。

translations.literal: " When Prince Wuling Ye held Kuaiji, the throne carefully chose staff for him, appointing Huxiao Merit Officer of the Punitive Campaign against the Barbarians, and he took up his post together with the prince's aide Liu Qin of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: " When Prince Wuling Ye governed Kuaiji, the court carefully chose his staff, made Huxiao merit officer of the punitive campaign against the barbarians, and he took up his post together with the prince's aide Liu Qin of Pei.

sentences.zh: 璡清介士也，行至吳，謂人曰：「吾聞張融與慧曉並宅，其間有水，此必有異味。

translations.literal: Qin was an upright man. When he reached Wu he told people: "I have heard that Zhang Rong and Huxiao live on adjoining estates with water between them; it must have a special savor.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was an upright man. When he reached Wu he said: "I hear Zhang Rong and Huxiao live side by side with water between them; it must have a special savor.

sentences.zh: 」故命駕往酌而飲之。

translations.literal: " So he ordered his carriage, went to draw from it, and drank.
translations.idiomatic: " So he had his carriage brought, went to draw from it, and drank.

sentences.zh: 曰：「飲此水，則鄙吝之萌盡矣。」

translations.literal: He said: "Drink this water and every trace of meanness is gone."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Drink this water and every trace of meanness is gone."

sentences.zh: 何點薦慧曉于豫章王嶷，補司空掾，加以恩禮。

translations.literal: He Dian recommended Huxiao to Prince Yuzhang of Yuzhang, who appointed him aide to the Minister of Works and treated him with favor.
translations.idiomatic: He Dian recommended Huxiao to Prince Yuzhang Ye, who made him aide to the minister of works and treated him with special favor.

sentences.zh: 累遷安西諮議、領冠軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He rose in due course to Adviser of the Pacification of the West and concurrently Recorder of the Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to adviser of the pacification of the west and concurrently recorder under the champion general.

sentences.zh: 武帝第三子廬陵王子卿為南豫州刺史，帝稱其小名謂司徒竟陵王子良曰：「烏熊癡如熊，不得天下第一人為行事，無以壓一州。

translations.literal: The Emperor's third son, Prince Ziqing of Luling, was made Governor of Southern Yuzhou. The Emperor used his childhood name and told the Minister of Works, Prince Ziliang of Jingling: "Black Bear is dull as a bear; unless the foremost man in the realm acts for him, he cannot hold down a province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's third son, Prince Ziqing of Luling, was made governor of southern Yuzhou. The emperor used his childhood name and told minister of works Prince Ziliang of Jingling: "Black Bear is dull as a bear; unless the foremost man in the realm runs affairs for him, he cannot hold down a province.

sentences.zh: 」既而曰：「吾思得人矣。

translations.literal: " Then he said: "I believe I have found the man.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he said: "I believe I have found the man.

sentences.zh: 」乃使慧曉為長史、行事。

translations.literal: " He then made Huxiao Chief Clerk with authority to act.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made Huxiao chief clerk with authority to act.

sentences.zh: 別帝，問曰：「卿何以輔持廬陵？

translations.literal: When he took leave of the Emperor, the throne asked: "How will you support Luling?
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave of the emperor, the throne asked: "How will you support Luling?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「靜以修身，儉以養性。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Through stillness to cultivate the person, through frugality to nurture the nature.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "Through stillness to cultivate the person, through frugality to nurture the nature.

sentences.zh: 靜則人不擾，儉則人不煩。

translations.literal: When there is stillness, people are not disturbed; when there is frugality, people are not wearied.
translations.idiomatic: When there is stillness, people are not disturbed; when there is frugality, people are not wearied.

sentences.zh: 」上大悅。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He later served as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later became right chief clerk under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 時陳郡謝朏為左長史，府公竟陵王子良謂王融曰：「我府前世誰比？

translations.literal: At the time Xie Tiao of Chen Commandery was Left Chief Clerk. The prince of the establishment, Ziliang of Jingling, asked Wang Rong: "To whom in former ages can my household be compared?
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiao of Chen commandery was then left chief clerk. Prince Ziliang of Jingling asked Wang Rong: "To whom in former ages can my household be compared?

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「明公二上佐，天下英奇，古來少見其比。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Your Grace's two chief aides are the finest men under heaven; seldom in antiquity has their like been seen.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong said: "Your Grace's two chief aides are the finest men under heaven; seldom in antiquity has their like been seen.

sentences.zh: 」子良西邸抄書，令慧曉參知其事。

translations.literal: " Ziliang had books copied at his Western Lodge and put Huxiao in charge of the work.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziliang had books copied at his western lodge and put Huxiao in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 建武初，除西中郎長史，行事、內史如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Western Central Guard, retaining his authority to act and his post as Interior Governor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jianwu he was made chief clerk of the western central guard, retaining his authority to act and his post as interior governor.

sentences.zh: 俄征黃門郎，未拜，遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; before he could take up the post he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as gentleman of the yellow gate; before he could assume office he was made director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王晏選門生補內外要局，慧曉為用數人而止。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wang Yan chose his disciples to fill important posts inside and outside the court; Huxiao appointed only a few and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of works Wang Yan chose his disciples to fill important posts inside and outside the court; Huxiao appointed only a few and stopped.

sentences.zh: 晏恨之。

translations.literal: Yan resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan resented him.

sentences.zh: 送女妓一人，欲與申好，慧曉不納。

translations.literal: He sent one female entertainer, wishing to establish friendly ties; Huxiao would not accept her.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a female entertainer, wishing to establish friendly ties; Huxiao would not accept her.

sentences.zh: 吏曹都令史曆政來諮執選事，慧曉任己獨行，未嘗與語。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Personnel Bureau Li Zheng came to consult on selections; Huxiao acted on his own authority and never spoke with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk of the personnel bureau Li Zheng came to consult on selections; Huxiao acted on his own authority and never spoke with him.

sentences.zh: 帝遣主書單景雋謂曰：「都令史諳悉舊貫，可共參懷。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Chief Secretary Shan Jingjun to say: "The chief clerk knows the old precedents well; you may consult with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent chief secretary Shan Jingjun to say: "The chief clerk knows the old precedents well; you may consult with him.

sentences.zh: 」慧曉謂景雋曰：「六十之年，不復能諮都令史為吏部郎也。

translations.literal: " Huxiao told Jingjun: "At sixty I can no longer consult the chief clerk in order to serve as Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: " Huxiao told Jingjun: "At sixty I can no longer consult the chief clerk in order to serve as director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 上若謂身不堪，便當拂衣而退。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty thinks me unfit, I shall shake out my robes and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty thinks me unfit, I shall shake out my robes and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚憚之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor feared him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor feared him greatly.

sentences.zh: 後欲用為侍中，以形短小乃止。

translations.literal: Later they wished to make him Palace Attendant, but stopped because he was short in stature.
translations.idiomatic: Later they wished to make him palace attendant, but stopped because he was short in stature.

sentences.zh: 出為晉安王鎮北司馬、征北長史、東海太守，行府州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Pacification of the North Major of Prince Jin'an, Chief Clerk of the Northern Campaign, and Governor of Donghai, with authority over the princely establishment and the province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as pacification of the north major under Prince Jin'an, chief clerk of the northern campaign, and governor of Donghai, with authority over the princely establishment and the province.

sentences.zh: 入為五兵尚書，行揚州事。

translations.literal: He entered court as Minister of the Five Armies and acted for Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as minister of the five armies and acted for Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景事平，領右軍將軍。

translations.literal: After Cui Huijing's affair was settled, he concurrently held the post of General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Huijing's affair was settled, he concurrently held the post of general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 出監南徐州。

translations.literal: He went out to oversee Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to oversee southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝議又欲以為侍中，王亮曰：「濟、河須人，今且就朝廷借之，以鎮南兗州。

translations.literal: Court discussion again favored making him Palace Attendant. Wang Liang said: "Ji and He need men; for now let us borrow him from the court to secure Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion again favored making him palace attendant. Wang Liang said: "Ji and He need men; for now let us borrow him from the court to secure southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 」王瑩、王志皆曰：「侍中彌須英華，方鎮猶應有選者。

translations.literal: " Wang Ying and Wang Zhi both said: "The palace attendant post especially requires brilliance; for a frontier command there should still be a choice.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Ying and Wang Zhi both said: "The palace attendant post especially requires brilliance; for a frontier command there should still be a choice.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「角其二者，則貂璫緩，拒寇切。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "Weigh the two: the court cap and scepter can wait, but repelling the enemy is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said: "Weigh the two: the court cap and scepter can wait, but repelling the enemy is urgent.

sentences.zh: 當今朝廷甚弱，宜從切者。

translations.literal: The court today is very weak; we should follow what is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The court today is very weak; we should follow what is urgent.

sentences.zh: 」乃以為輔國將軍、南兗州刺史，加督。

translations.literal: " He was therefore made Assisting-State General and Governor of Southern Yanzhou with supervisory powers.
translations.idiomatic: " He was therefore made assisting-state general and governor of southern Yanzhou with supervisory powers.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，俄爾以疾歸。

translations.literal: When he reached his post he soon returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached his post he soon returned home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 三子：僚、任、倕並有美名，時人謂之三陸。

translations.literal: His three sons—Liao, Ren, and Chui—all had fine reputations; people of the time called them the Three Lus.
translations.idiomatic: His three sons—Liao, Ren, and Chui—all had fine reputations; people of the day called them the Three Lus.

sentences.zh: 初授慧曉兗州，三子依次第各作一讓表，辭並雅麗，時人歎伏。

translations.literal: When Huxiao was first appointed to Yanzhou, the three sons in turn each drafted a memorial declining the honor; the language was elegant throughout, and contemporaries sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Huxiao was first appointed to Yanzhou, the three sons in turn each drafted a memorial declining the honor; the language was elegant throughout, and contemporaries sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 僚學涉子史，長於微言。

translations.literal: Liao studied the Masters and histories and excelled in subtle doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Liao read widely in the Masters and histories and had a gift for subtle argument.

sentences.zh: 美姿容，鬚眉如畫。

translations.literal: He had handsome looks; his beard and brows were like a painting.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome, with beard and brows as finely drawn as in a portrait.

sentences.zh: 位西昌侯長史、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Chief Administrator to the Marquis of Xichang and Governor of Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief administrator to the Marquis of Xichang and as governor of Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 倕字佐公，少勤學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Chui, style name Zuogong, from youth applied himself to study and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Chui, styled Zuogong, studied hard from boyhood and wrote with real skill.

sentences.zh: 於宅內起兩茅屋，杜絕往來，晝夜讀書，如此者數歲。

translations.literal: Within his house he built two thatched huts, cut off all visitors, and read day and night in this way for several years.
translations.idiomatic: He built two thatched huts in his courtyard, shut out all callers, and read day and night like this for years.

sentences.zh: 所讀一遍，必誦於口。

translations.literal: Whatever he read once, he always recited aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he read through once, he recited aloud from memory.

sentences.zh: 嘗借人漢書，失五行志四卷，乃暗寫還之，略無遺脫。

translations.literal: Once he borrowed someone's Book of Han and lost four scrolls of the Treatise on the Five Phases; he copied them out from memory in secret and returned them, with scarcely a word missing.
translations.idiomatic: Once he borrowed a Book of Han and lost four scrolls of the Treatise on the Five Phases; he secretly copied them out from memory and returned the book, scarcely a word missing.

sentences.zh: 幼為外祖張岱所異。

translations.literal: In childhood he was regarded as extraordinary by his maternal grandfather Zhang Dai.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he struck his maternal grandfather Zhang Dai as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 岱嘗謂諸子曰：「此兒，汝家陽元也。

translations.literal: Dai once said to his sons: "This boy is your family's yang luminance.
translations.idiomatic: Dai once told his sons, "This boy is the yang force of your house.

sentences.zh: 」十七，舉本州秀才。

translations.literal: " At seventeen he was recommended as a provincial talent.
translations.idiomatic: " At seventeen he was nominated as a provincial talent.

sentences.zh: 刺史竟陵王子良開西邸，延英俊，倕預焉。

translations.literal: The Inspector, Prince Ziliang of Jingling, opened the Western Residence and gathered men of talent; Chui was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the inspector, Prince Ziliang of Jingling, opened his Western Residence and gathered brilliant men, Chui was invited.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，為右軍安成王主簿，與樂安任昉友，為感知己賦以贈昉，昉因此名以報之。

translations.literal: In the early Tianjian era of Liang he served as secretary to Prince Ancheng of the Right Army, befriended Ren Fang of Le'an, and wrote an "Ode on Sensing a True Friend" to present to Fang; Fang repaid him with a piece titled in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianjian reign of Liang he was secretary to Prince Ancheng of the Right Army, became friends with Ren Fang of Le'an, and wrote an "Ode on Sensing a True Friend" for him; Fang answered with a piece named in his turn.

sentences.zh: 及昉為中丞，簪裾輻湊，預其燕者，殷芸、到溉、劉苞、劉孺、劉顯、劉孝綽及倕而已，號曰：「龍門之遊。

translations.literal: When Fang became Inspectorate Censor-in-Chief, officials in caps and robes crowded in; those who shared his banquets were only Yin Yun, Dao Gai, Liu Bao, Liu Ru, Liu Xian, Liu Xiaochuo, and Chui—they were called the "Gatherings at Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang became censor-in-chief, officials thronged about him; only Yin Yun, Dao Gai, Liu Bao, Liu Ru, Liu Xian, Liu Xiaochuo, and Chui were admitted to his gatherings—they called themselves the "Gatherings at Dragon Gate."

sentences.zh: 」雖貴公子孫不得預也。

translations.literal: " Even sons of noble houses could not join.
translations.idiomatic: " Even sons of the highest families were not admitted.

sentences.zh: 遷臨川王東曹掾。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Eastern Bureau Aide to the Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made eastern bureau aide to the Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝雅愛倕才，乃敕撰新漏刻銘，其文甚美。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang greatly admired Chui's talent and ordered him to compose an inscription for the new clepsydra; the text was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang admired Chui's talent and ordered him to write an inscription for the new water clock; the piece was superb.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中舍人，又詔為石闕銘，敕褒美之，賜絹三十匹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Crown Prince, then again ordered to write an inscription for the stone gate-tower; the throne praised it and bestowed thirty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant-in-ordinary to the crown prince, then was ordered to write an inscription for the stone gate-tower; the throne praised the work and gave him thirty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常卿，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in due course to Minister of Ceremonies and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to minister of ceremonies and died.

sentences.zh: 子纘早慧，七歲通經，為童子郎，卒。

translations.literal: His son Zuan was precocious; at seven he had mastered the classics and was made a Youth Attendant, then died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuan was brilliant early; at seven he knew the classics, was made a youth attendant, and died.

sentences.zh: 次緬，有似於倕，一看殆不能別。

translations.literal: Next was Mian, who resembled Chui so closely that at a glance one could scarcely tell them apart.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Mian, who looked so like Chui that at a glance one could hardly tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 繕字士繻，倕兄子也。

translations.literal: Shan, style name Shirui, was Chui's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Shan, styled Shirui, was Chui's nephew.

sentences.zh: 父任，御史中丞。

translations.literal: His father Ren served as Inspectorate Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren had been censor-in-chief of the inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 繕幼有志尚，以雅正知名。

translations.literal: From youth Shan had high aspirations and was known for elegant rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Shan had high aspirations from youth and was known for refined integrity.

sentences.zh: 梁承聖中，為中書侍郎，掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: In the Chengsheng era of Liang he served as Secretariat Vice Director and managed the Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chengsheng era of Liang he was vice director of the Secretariat and kept the crown prince's records.

sentences.zh: 魏平江陵，繕微服遁還建鄴。

translations.literal: When Wei took Jiangling, Shan fled in disguise back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei captured Jiangling, Shan slipped away in plain dress and made his way back to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 後復拜御史中丞，猶以父所終，固辭，不許，乃權換廨宇，徙以居之。

translations.literal: Later he was again appointed Inspectorate Censor-in-Chief, but because his father had died in that office he firmly declined; when this was not allowed, he temporarily exchanged offices and moved to live in the other one.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again made censor-in-chief, but since his father had died in that post he firmly declined; when the court would not hear of it, he arranged a temporary swap of offices and moved into his father's old quarters.

sentences.zh: 太建中，曆度支尚書，侍中，太子詹事，尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he successively held the posts of Minister of Revenue, Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he served in turn as minister of revenue, palace attendant, grand tutor of the crown prince, and right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左僕射，參掌選事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Vice Director and took part in managing appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left vice director and helped manage personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 別敕與徐陵等七人參議政事。

translations.literal: By special edict he joined Xu Ling and six others in deliberating on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict he joined Xu Ling and six others in deliberating state affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈特進，諡曰安子。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Special Grand Master; his posthumous name was Anzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made special grand master with the posthumous name Anzi.

sentences.zh: 以繕東宮舊臣，特賜祖奠。

translations.literal: Because Shan had been an old Eastern Palace official, he was specially granted an ancestral funeral rite.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shan had been an old crown prince official, the court specially granted him an ancestral funeral ceremony.

sentences.zh: 繕子辯慧，年數歲，詔引入殿內，進止有父風，宣帝因賜名辯慧字敬仁。

translations.literal: Shan's son Bianhui, only a few years old, was summoned by edict into the palace; his bearing had his father's manner, and Emperor Xuan therefore bestowed the name Bianhui with the style Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's son, only a few years old, was summoned into the palace by edict; his bearing recalled his father's, and Emperor Xuan therefore gave him the name Bianhui and the style Jingren.

sentences.zh: 繕兄子見賢亦方雅，位少府卿，卒。

translations.literal: Shan's nephew Jianxian was also upright and refined; he reached the post of Minister Steward and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's nephew Jianxian was likewise upright and refined; he rose to minister steward and died.

sentences.zh: 閑字遐業，慧曉兄子也。

translations.literal: Xian, style name Xiaye, was a nephew of Huxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, styled Xiaye, was Huxiao's nephew.

sentences.zh: 有風概，與人交不苟合，少為同郡張緒所知。

translations.literal: He had force of character; in dealings with others he would not join company lightly, and in youth he was noticed by Zhang Xu of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He had real force of character, would not make friends lightly, and in youth won the notice of Zhang Xu of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 仕至揚州別駕。

translations.literal: In office he rose to Vice Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in office to vice governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝崩，閑謂所親人曰：「宮車晏駕，百司將聽塚宰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Qi died, Xian said to those close to him: "The imperial carriage has halted at dusk; the hundred offices will heed the grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Qi died, Xian told those close to him, "The emperor is gone; the hundred offices will now look to the regent.

sentences.zh: 主王地重才弱，必不能振，難將至矣。

translations.literal: The young prince holds great territory but weak talent; he surely cannot restore order—trouble is coming.
translations.idiomatic: The young prince holds heavy power but has little strength; he will never set things right—trouble is coming.

sentences.zh: 」乃感心疾，不復預州事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took to heart sickness and no longer attended to prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He then feigned heart sickness and withdrew from prefectural business.

sentences.zh: 永元末，刺史始安王遙光據東府作亂，或勸去之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongyuan era the Inspector, Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an, seized the Eastern Residence and rebelled; some urged Xian to leave.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongyuan the governor, Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an, seized the Eastern Residence and rebelled; some urged Xian to flee.

sentences.zh: 閑曰：「吾為人吏，何可逃死。

translations.literal: Xian said: "I serve as another's officer—how could I flee from death?
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "I am another man's officer—how can I run from death?"

sentences.zh: 」台軍攻陷城，閑以綱佐被收，至杜姥宅，尚書令徐孝嗣啟閑不預逆謀。

translations.literal: " The imperial army stormed the city; Xian, as a subordinate aide, was arrested and taken to Old Woman Du's house; Chief Minister Xu Xiaosi memorialized that Xian had not joined the plot.
translations.idiomatic: " When the imperial army took the city, Xian was seized as a subordinate aide and taken to Old Woman Du's house; Chief Minister Xu Xiaosi reported that Xian had taken no part in the plot.

sentences.zh: 未及報，徐世標命殺之。

translations.literal: Before a reply came, Xu Shibiao ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the reply arrived, Xu Shibiao ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 閑四子：厥、絳、完、襄也。

translations.literal: Xian had four sons: Jue, Jiang, Wan, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had four sons: Jue, Jiang, Wan, and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 絳字魏卿，時隨閑，抱頸求代死，不獲，遂以身蔽刀刃，行刑者俱害之。

translations.literal: Jiang, style name Weiqing, was then with Xian; he clutched his neck and begged to die in his place, was refused, then shielded him with his body from the blades, and the executioners killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, styled Weiqing, was with Xian at the time; he threw his arms around his father's neck and begged to die in his stead, and when this was refused he covered him with his body—so the executioners killed them both.

sentences.zh: 厥字韓卿，少有風概，好屬文。

translations.literal: Jue, style name Hanqing, from youth had force of character and loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Jue, styled Hanqing, had force of character from youth and loved to write.

sentences.zh: 齊永明九年，詔百官舉士，同郡司徒左西曹掾顧暠之表薦厥，州舉秀才。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming of Qi an edict ordered all officials to recommend men of talent; Gu Huozhi, Western Bureau Aide on the Left of the Minister of Works in the same commandery, memorialized recommending Jue, and the province recommended him as a talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongming of Qi the throne ordered officials to recommend talent; Gu Huozhi, western bureau aide on the left of the minister of works in the same commandery, memorialized in Jue's favor, and the province nominated him as a talent.

sentences.zh: 時盛為文章，吳興沈約、陳郡謝朓、琅邪王融以氣類相推轂，汝南周顒善識聲韻。

translations.literal: At the time literary composition was in vogue; Shen Yue of Wuxing, Xie Tiao of Chen commandery, and Wang Rong of Langya promoted one another as kindred spirits, and Zhou Yong of Runan was skilled at discerning tones and rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Literary composition was then at its height; Shen Yue of Wuxing, Xie Tiao of Chen commandery, and Wang Rong of Langya urged one another on as kindred spirits, and Zhou Yong of Runan had a keen ear for tone and rhyme.

sentences.zh: 約等文皆用宮商，將平上去入四聲，以此制韻，有平頭、上尾、蜂腰、鶴膝。

translations.literal: The writings of Yue and the others all employed gong and shang; they would harmonize the four tones—level, rising, departing, and entering—and by this rule their rhyme, producing flat-head, upper-tail, wasp-waist, and crane-knee faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and the others wrote with gong-shang tonal patterning, arranging the four tones—level, rising, departing, and entering—to govern rhyme, with faults called flat-head, upper-tail, wasp-waist, and crane-knee.

sentences.zh: 五字之中，音韻悉異，兩句之內，角征不同，不可增減。

translations.literal: Within five characters all tones were different; within two lines jue and zhi were not the same; nothing could be added or removed.
translations.idiomatic: Within five characters every tone had to differ; within two lines jue and zhi could not match; not a word could be added or dropped.

sentences.zh: 世呼為「永明體」。

translations.literal: The age called this the "Yongming Style."
translations.idiomatic: People of the age called this the "Yongming style."

sentences.zh: 沈約宋書謝靈運傳後又論其事，厥與約書曰：

translations.literal: Shen Yue, after his discussion of the matter in the Song Shu biography of Xie Lingyun, received a letter from Jue saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Shen Yue discussed the matter in his Song Shu biography of Xie Lingyun, Jue wrote to him:

sentences.zh: 范詹事自序：「性別宮商，識清濁，特能適輕重，濟艱難。

translations.literal: Minister of the Household Fan's preface says: "By nature I distinguish gong and shang, know clear from muddy, and am especially able to fit light and heavy and overcome difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Household Fan writes in his preface, "By nature I distinguish gong from shang and clear from muddy tones, and I am especially able to balance weight and ease difficulty.

sentences.zh: 古今文人多不全了斯處，縱有會此者，不必從根本中來。

translations.literal: Writers ancient and modern for the most part do not fully grasp this point; even those who sometimes hit upon it need not have arrived at it from the root.
translations.idiomatic: Most writers ancient and modern never fully grasp this; even those who sometimes hit upon it need not have reached it from the root.

sentences.zh: 」尚書亦云：「自靈均以來，此秘未睹。

translations.literal: " The Minister of Rites also said: "Since Qu Yuan, this secret has never been seen.
translations.idiomatic: " The Minister of Rites also says, "Since Qu Yuan, this secret has never been seen.

sentences.zh: 或暗與理合，匪由思至。

translations.literal: Some dimly accord with principle, not because thought brought them there.
translations.idiomatic: Some dimly accord with principle, not because thought led them there.

sentences.zh: 張、蔡、曹、王曾無先覺，潘、陸、顏、謝去之彌遠。

translations.literal: Zhang, Cai, Cao, and Wang never had prior insight; Pan, Lu, Yan, and Xie fell ever farther from it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Cai, Cao, and Wang never saw it first; Pan, Lu, Yan, and Xie fell ever farther away.

sentences.zh: 」大旨欲「宮商相變，低昂舛節，若前有浮聲，則後須切響，一簡之內，音韻盡殊，兩句之中，輕重悉異」。

translations.literal: The gist was that "gong and shang should alternate, high and low should clash in rhythm; if the earlier line has a floating tone, the later must have a sharp echo; within one line all tones must differ, and within two lines all weight must differ."
translations.idiomatic: The gist was that "gong and shang must alternate, pitch must rise and fall in counterpoint; if the first line carries a floating tone, the next must answer with a sharp one; within a single line every tone must differ, and within two lines every stress must differ."

sentences.zh: 辭既美矣，理又善焉；

translations.literal: The language was already beautiful, and the principle good as well;
translations.idiomatic: The language was already fine, and the principle sound as well;

sentences.zh: 但觀歷代眾賢似不都闇此處，而云：「此秘未睹」，近於誣乎。

translations.literal: but looking at worthy men of every age, they do not all seem wholly ignorant of this point—so to say "this secret has never been seen" comes close to slander, does it not?
translations.idiomatic: but looking at the worthy writers of every age, they hardly seem wholly blind to this—so to say "this secret has never been seen" comes close to slander, does it not?

sentences.zh: 案范云：「不從根本中來」，尚書云：「匪由思至」，斯則揣情謬于玄黃，擿句著其音律也。

translations.literal: Consider Fan's words, "not from the root," and the Minister of Rites' words, "not because thought brought one there"—this is to infer feeling wrongly in dark-and-yellow mysteries and to pick out lines to display their tonal pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Fan says, "not from the root"; the Minister of Rites says, "not because thought brought one there"—that is to misread feeling in cosmic terms and to pick out lines only to show off their tonal pattern.

sentences.zh: 范又云：「時有會此者」，尚書云：「或闇與理合」。

translations.literal: Fan also says, "sometimes one hits upon it," and the Minister of Rites says, "sometimes one dimly accords with principle."
translations.idiomatic: Fan also says, "sometimes one hits upon it"; the Minister of Rites says, "sometimes one dimly accords with principle."

sentences.zh: 則美詠清謳，有辭章調韻者，雖有差謬，亦有會合。

translations.literal: Then in fine songs and clear lyrics, wherever there is phrasing and tonal harmony, though there are errors, there are also points of accord.
translations.idiomatic: Then in fine songs and clear lyrics, wherever phrasing and rhyme meet, even with faults there are also points of accord.

sentences.zh: 推此以往，可得而言。

translations.literal: Push this reasoning onward and one may speak further.
translations.idiomatic: Push the argument further and the case can be stated plainly.

sentences.zh: 夫思有合離，前哲同所不免，文有開塞，即事不得無之。

translations.literal: Thought has its unions and partings, which even sages of old could not wholly escape; writing has its openings and blockages, which no undertaking can be without.
translations.idiomatic: Thought has its unions and partings, which even the sages of old could not escape; writing has its openings and blockages, which no work can lack.

sentences.zh: 子建所以好人譏彈，士衡所以遺恨終篇。

translations.literal: This is why Zijian was often mocked by others, and why Shiheng left regret at the end of his piece.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Cao Zijian drew mockery from others, and why Lu Shiheng ended a piece with regret.

sentences.zh: 既曰遺恨，非盡美之作。

translations.literal: If one speaks of leaving regret, it is not a wholly perfect work.
translations.idiomatic: If a work ends in regret, it is not a wholly perfect piece.

sentences.zh: 理可詆訶，君子執其詆訶，便謂合理為闇，豈如指其合理，而寄詆訶為遺恨邪。

translations.literal: The principle may be faulted; if a gentleman seizes on the faulting and then calls what was reasonable obscure, how is that like pointing to what was reasonable and treating the faulting as regret?
translations.idiomatic: Principle may be faulted; if a gentleman seizes on the fault and then calls what was sound obscure, how is that like pointing to what was sound and treating the fault as regret?

sentences.zh: 自魏文屬論，深以清濁為言，劉楨奏書，大明體勢之致。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wen of Wei's essay onward, clear and muddy tones were deeply discussed; Liu Zhen's memorial clearly set forth the reach of form and momentum.
translations.idiomatic: From Cao Pi's essay onward, clear and muddy tones were deeply discussed; Liu Zhen's memorial clearly set forth the force of form and momentum.

sentences.zh: 齟齬妥怗之談，操末續巔之說，興玄黃於律呂，比五色之相宣。

translations.literal: Talk of jarring fit and smooth accord, discourse tying stem to peak, raising dark and yellow in pitch-pipes, comparing them to the mutual harmony of the five colors—
translations.idiomatic: Talk of jarring fit and smooth accord, discourse tying root to crown, raising dark and yellow in the pitch-pipes, comparing them to the harmony of the five colors—

sentences.zh: 苟此秘未睹，茲論為何所指邪？

translations.literal: if this secret had never been seen, what were those discussions pointing to?
translations.idiomatic: if this secret had never been seen, what were those discussions about?

sentences.zh: 愚謂前英已早識宮征，但未屈曲指的，若今論所申。

translations.literal: I foolishly think that earlier masters already knew jue and zhi early on, but simply did not bend and point it out as explicitly as the present discussion declares.
translations.idiomatic: I think the earlier masters already knew jue and zhi long ago, but simply did not bend every detail to point it out as explicitly as your discussion does.

sentences.zh: 至於掩瑕藏疾，合少謬多，則臨淄所云：「人之著述，不能無病。

translations.literal: As for hiding flaws and concealing faults, with few fits and many errors, this is what the man of Linzi said: "In human writing there can be no work without faults.
translations.idiomatic: As for hiding flaws and concealing faults, with few fits and many errors—that is what the man of Linzi said: "In human writing there can be no work without faults.

sentences.zh: 」者也。
非知之而不改，謂不改則不知，斯曹、陸又稱「竭情多悔，不可力強。

translations.literal: It is not that they knew yet did not change; to say they did not change is to say they did not know—this is what Cao and Lu also meant by "exhaust feeling and there is much regret; it cannot be forced by strength.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that they knew and would not change; not to change is not to know—that is what Cao and Lu also meant by "pour out feeling and regret is plentiful; it cannot be forced by strength.

sentences.zh: 」者也。
今許以有病有悔為言，則必自知無悔無病之地。

translations.literal: If one now grants that there are faults and regrets in speaking, then one must oneself know the ground where there is no regret and no fault.
translations.idiomatic: If one now speaks of faults and regrets, one must already know the ground where there is no regret and no fault.

sentences.zh: 引其不了不合為闇，何獨誣其一合一了之明乎？

translations.literal: To cite what was incomplete or unfitting as obscurity—why slander only their one point of accord and one point of mastery?
translations.idiomatic: To cite what was incomplete or unfitting as obscurity—why slander only their one point of accord, their one point of mastery?

sentences.zh: 意者亦質文時異，今古好殊，將急在情物，而緩於章句。

translations.literal: I suspect that substance and ornament differ with the age, and ancient and modern tastes diverge; the urgent concern was feeling and object, while phrasing was treated more lightly.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect substance and ornament differ by age and ancient and modern tastes diverge; the urgent concern was feeling and object, while phrasing was treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 情物，文之所急，美惡猶且相半；

translations.literal: Feeling and object are what writing urgently seeks; beauty and ugliness are still half and half;
translations.idiomatic: Feeling and object are what writing urgently seeks, and beauty and ugliness are still half and half;

sentences.zh: 章句，意之所緩，故合少而謬多。

translations.literal: phrasing is what meaning treats lightly, hence few fits and many errors.
translations.idiomatic: phrasing is what meaning treats lightly, hence few fits and many errors.

sentences.zh: 義兼於斯，必非不知明矣。

translations.literal: When meaning embraces both, they surely were not ignorant and unclear.
translations.idiomatic: When meaning embraces both, they surely were not ignorant.

sentences.zh: 長門、上林，殆非一家之賦，洛神、池雁，便成二體之作。

translations.literal: Changmen and Shanglin are almost not the fu of one house; Luoshen and Chiyan became works of two styles.
translations.idiomatic: Changmen and Shanglin are scarcely the work of one hand; Luoshen and Chiyan became two different styles.

sentences.zh: 孟堅精正，詠史無虧於東主，平子恢富，羽獵不累於憑虛。

translations.literal: Mengjian was precise and upright; Singing History in no way fell short of the Eastern Lord; Pingzi was grand and rich, and Hunting Rhapsody does not lag behind On the Void.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Mengjian was precise and upright, and his Historical Odes in no way fell short of the eastern patron; Zhang Pingzi was grand and rich, and his Hunting Rhapsody does not lag behind On the Void.

sentences.zh: 王粲初征，他文未能稱是，楊修敏捷，暑賦彌日不獻。

translations.literal: Wang Can's First Journey—his other writings could not match it; Yang Xiu was quick-witted, yet his Summer Rhapsody took days and was never submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Can's First Journey—his other pieces could not match it; Yang Xiu was quick-witted, yet his Summer Rhapsody took days and was never submitted.

sentences.zh: 率意寡尤，則事促乎一日，翳翳愈伏，而理賒于七步。

translations.literal: Write freely with few faults, and the task is hurried within a day; grow ever more obscure and hidden, and the reasoning stretches to seven paces.
translations.idiomatic: Write freely with few faults and the work is done in a day; grow ever more obscure and hidden and the reasoning stretches to seven paces.

sentences.zh: 一人之思，遲速天懸，一家之文，工拙壤隔，何獨宮商律呂必責其如一邪？

translations.literal: One person's thought, fast or slow, is separated as heaven; one family's writings, skilled or clumsy, are separated as earth—why must gong-shang pitch-pipes alone be forced to uniformity?
translations.idiomatic: One person's thought may be swift or slow as heaven and earth apart; one family's writings may be skilled or clumsy worlds apart—why demand that gong-shang pitch-pipes alone be uniform?

sentences.zh: 論者乃可言未窮其致，不得言曾無先覺也。

translations.literal: Critics may say the reach has not been fully exhausted, but they may not say there was never prior insight.
translations.idiomatic: Critics may say the reach has not been fully exhausted, but they may not say there was never prior insight.

sentences.zh: 約答曰：

translations.literal: Yue replied:
translations.idiomatic: Yue replied:

sentences.zh: 宮商之聲有五，文字之別累萬。

translations.literal: The sounds of gong and shang are five; the distinctions among written characters number in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The sounds of gong and shang are five; the distinctions among written characters number in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 以累萬之繁，配五聲之約，高下低昂，非思力所學，又非止若斯而已。

translations.literal: To match tens of thousands of complexities to the restraint of five sounds—high, low, light, and heavy—is not something thought alone can learn, and it does not stop even there.
translations.idiomatic: To match tens of thousands of complexities to the restraint of five tones—high, low, light, and heavy—is not something thought alone can master, and that is not all.

sentences.zh: 十字之文，顛倒相配，字不過十，巧曆已不能盡，何況復過於此者乎？

translations.literal: In a text of ten characters, reversed and paired, the characters are no more than ten; even a clever reckoner cannot exhaust them—how much less when they exceed this?
translations.idiomatic: In a text of ten characters, reversed and paired, there are no more than ten characters; even a clever reckoner cannot exhaust the combinations—how much less when there are more?

sentences.zh: 靈均以來，未經用之於懷抱，固無從得其髣佛矣。

translations.literal: Since Qu Yuan, it has never been applied in one's own breast, so there is truly no way to catch even its likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qu Yuan, no one has truly applied it in his own breast, so there is no way even to catch its likeness.

sentences.zh: 若斯之妙，而聖人不尚，何耶？

translations.literal: If the art is so marvelous, yet the sages did not esteem it—why?
translations.idiomatic: If the art is so marvelous, yet the sages did not esteem it—why?

sentences.zh: 此蓋曲折聲韻之巧，無當於訓義，非聖哲玄言之所急也，是以子雲譬之「雕蟲篆刻」，云：「壯夫不為」。

translations.literal: This is because the subtlety of bent tonal pattern has no bearing on doctrinal meaning; it is not what sage and philosopher in their profound discourse urgently seek—therefore Ziyun compared it to "carving insects and seal script," saying, "A full-grown man does not do it."
translations.idiomatic: This is because the subtlety of bent tonal pattern has no bearing on doctrinal meaning; it is not what sages and philosophers urgently seek in profound discourse—therefore Yang Ziyun compared it to "carving insects and seal script" and said, "A full-grown man does not do it."

sentences.zh: 自古辭人豈不知宮羽之殊、商征之別。

translations.literal: Writers of old—did they not know the difference between gong and yu, shang and zhi?
translations.idiomatic: Writers of old—did they not know gong from yu, shang from zhi?

sentences.zh: 雖知五音之異，而其中參差變動，所昧實多，故鄙意所謂「此秘未睹。

translations.literal: Though one knows the five tones differ, the shifting gradations within them remain much obscure—hence my humble view's "this secret has never been seen.
translations.idiomatic: Though one knows the five tones differ, the shifting gradations within them remain much obscure—hence my humble view that "this secret has never been seen.

sentences.zh: 」者也。
以此而推，則知前世文士，便未悟此處。

translations.literal: Pushing this reasoning onward, one knows that writers of earlier ages simply had not grasped this point.
translations.idiomatic: Push this reasoning onward and one sees that writers of earlier ages simply had not grasped this point.

sentences.zh: 若以文章之音韻，同弦管之聲曲，美惡妍蚩，不得頓相乖反，譬猶子野操曲，安得忽有闡緩失調之聲。

translations.literal: If the tonal pattern of literary composition is the same as the sound and melody of string and pipe, then beauty and ugliness, fair and foul, cannot suddenly turn contrary—just as when Ziye plays a tune, how could there suddenly be a slow, off-key note?
translations.idiomatic: If the tonal pattern of literary composition is the same as the sound and melody of lute and pipe, then beauty and ugliness, fair and foul, cannot suddenly turn contrary—just as when Ziye plays a tune, how could there suddenly be a slow, off-key note?

sentences.zh: 以洛神比陳思他賦，有似異手之作，故知天機啟，則律呂自調，六情滯，則音律頓舛也。

translations.literal: Comparing Goddess of Luo with Prince Si's other fu, it seems like the work of different hands—thus one knows that when natural endowment opens, pitch-pipes self-adjust; when the six emotions stagnate, tone and rhythm suddenly err.
translations.idiomatic: Compare Goddess of Luo with Prince Si of Chen's other rhapsodies and they seem the work of different hands—when natural talent awakens, pitch and tone fall into place by themselves; when the six emotions stall, rhythm and rhyme suddenly go wrong.

sentences.zh: 士衡雖云煥若縟錦，寧有濯色江波，其中復有一片是衛文之服。

translations.literal: Though Shiheng said 'brilliant as brocade,' could there be colors washed in river waves, and among them still a piece of Duke Wen of Wei's garment?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shiheng said writing should be 'brilliant as brocade,' yet could brocade washed in river waves still contain a scrap of Duke Wen of Wei's shabby garment?

sentences.zh: 此則陸生之言，即復不盡者矣。

translations.literal: This is what Mr. Lu said, yet even that does not exhaust the matter.
translations.idiomatic: That is what Mr. Lu said—and even that does not exhaust the point.

sentences.zh: 韻與不韻，復有精粗，輪扁不能言之，老夫亦不盡辯此。

translations.literal: Rhyme and non-rhyme also have fine and coarse grades; Lun Bian could not put it into words, and this old man also cannot fully argue this.
translations.idiomatic: Rhyme and non-rhyme also have finer and coarser grades; Lun Bian could not put his craft into words, and this old man cannot fully debate the matter either.

sentences.zh: 約論四聲，妙有詮辯，而諸賦亦往往與聲韻乖。

translations.literal: Yue's discourse on the four tones has fine explication, yet the various fu also often clash with sound and rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue's discourse on the four tones is finely argued, yet the various rhapsodies also often clash with sound and rhyme.

sentences.zh: 時有王斌者，不知何許人。

translations.literal: At the time there was a Wang Bin, of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was a Wang Bin, and no one knew where he came from.

sentences.zh: 著《四聲論》行于時。

translations.literal: He wrote Discourse on the Four Tones, which circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Discourse on the Four Tones, which circulated at the time.

sentences.zh: 斌初為道人，博涉經籍，雅有才辯，善屬文，能唱導而不修容儀。

translations.literal: Bin was first a Daoist monk, broadly versed in the classics, naturally gifted in debate, skilled at composition, able to preach and guide but careless of appearance and deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had first been a Daoist monk. He read widely in the classics, was naturally gifted in debate, wrote well, and could preach and lead others, but paid no attention to dress or deportment.

sentences.zh: 嘗弊衣於瓦官寺聽雲法師講成實論，無復坐處，唯僧正慧超尚空席，斌直坐其側。

translations.literal: Once, in shabby clothes at Waguan Temple listening to Master Yun lecture on the Satyasiddhi Treatise, there was no seat left; only Abbot Huichao still had an empty seat, and Bin sat down directly beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, dressed in ragged clothes, he went to Waguan Temple to hear Master Yun lecture on the Satyasiddhi Treatise. Every seat was taken except one beside Abbot Huichao, and Bin simply sat down next to him.

sentences.zh: 慧超不能平，乃罵曰：「那得此道人，祿蔌似隊父唐突人。

translations.literal: Huichao could not accept it and cursed, saying: "How does this monk get here? Shabby as Duifu, he offends people rudely.
translations.idiomatic: Huichao could not bear it and cursed him: "What is this monk doing here? Ragged as Duifu, he rudely offends people.

sentences.zh: 」因命驅之。

translations.literal: " So he ordered him driven out.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered him thrown out.

sentences.zh: 斌笑曰：「既有敘勳僧正，何為無隊父道人。

translations.literal: Bin smiled and said: "Since there is an abbot who records merit, why should there not be a rough-shod monk?
translations.idiomatic: Bin smiled and said: "If there is an abbot who records merit, why should there not be a rough-shod monk too?

sentences.zh: 」不為動。

translations.literal: " He was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: " He did not budge.

sentences.zh: 而撫機問難，辭理清舉，四座皆屬目。

translations.literal: Then, taking up the debate, he raised difficulties; his language was clear and elegant, and everyone in the hall turned their eyes to him.
translations.idiomatic: Then he joined the discussion and pressed hard questions; his language was clear and polished, and everyone in the hall watched him.

sentences.zh: 後還俗，以詩樂自樂，人莫能名之。

translations.literal: Later he returned to lay life, taking pleasure in poetry and music for himself; no one could characterize his art.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to lay life and amused himself with poetry and music; no one could quite classify his talent.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，始安王遙光反，厥父閑被誅，厥坐系尚方。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan, the Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, rebelled; Jue's father Xian was executed, and Jue was imprisoned on charge at the imperial workshops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan the Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, rebelled. Jue's father Xian was executed, and Jue was imprisoned in the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 尋有赦，厥感慟而卒，年二十八。

translations.literal: Soon there was an amnesty, but Jue died of grief and anguish, aged twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty soon followed, but Jue died of grief, aged twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 時有會稽虞炎以文學與沈約俱為文惠太子所遇，意眄殊常，官至驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: At the time there was Yu Yan of Kuaiji, who for literary accomplishment together with Shen Yue received special favor from Crown Prince Wen Hui; his regard was extraordinary; he reached General of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yu Yan of Kuaiji, noted for literary talent, together with Shen Yue enjoyed extraordinary favor from Crown Prince Wen Hui and rose to General of the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 襄字師卿，厥第四弟也。

translations.literal: Xiang, style name Shiqing, was Jue's fourth younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, styled Shiqing, was Jue's fourth younger brother.

sentences.zh: 本名衰字趙卿，有奏事者誤字為襄，梁武帝乃改為襄字師卿。

translations.literal: His original name was Shuai, style name Zhaoqing; a memorialist mistakenly wrote the character as Xiang, and Emperor Wu of Liang therefore changed it to Xiang, style name Shiqing.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Shuai, styled Zhaoqing, but a memorialist mistakenly wrote the character as Xiang, so Emperor Wu of Liang changed it to Xiang, styled Shiqing.

sentences.zh: 天監三年，都官尚書范岫表薦襄，起家著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian, Fan Xiu, Minister of Justice, memorialized recommending Xiang; he began his career as Editorial Aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianjian, Fan Xiu, minister of justice, memorialized recommending Xiang, and he began his career as editorial aide.

sentences.zh: 後昭明太子統聞襄業行，啟武帝引與遊處。

translations.literal: Later Crown Prince Zhaoming, Tong, heard of Xiang's conduct and accomplishment and memorialized Emperor Wu to bring him into his company.
translations.idiomatic: Later Crown Prince Zhaoming, Tong, heard of Xiang's conduct and learning and asked Emperor Wu to bring him into his company.

sentences.zh: 自廬陵王記室除太子洗馬，遷中舍人，並掌管記。

translations.literal: From secretary of the Prince of Luling he was appointed Crown Prince's Groom, promoted to Palace Aide, and in both posts managed the diary.
translations.idiomatic: From secretary to the Prince of Luling he was appointed crown prince's groom, then promoted to palace aide; in both posts he managed the diary.

sentences.zh: 出為揚州中從事，以父終此官，固辭。

translations.literal: He went out as Yangzhou acting inspector; because his father had died in that office, he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as acting inspector of Yangzhou, but because his father had died in that post he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 武帝不許，聽與府司馬換廨居之。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not allow it but permitted him to exchange offices with the prefectural aide and live in that residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, but allowed him to swap offices with the prefectural aide and live in that residence instead.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子敬耆老，襄母年將八十，與蕭琛、傅昭、陸杲每月常遣存問，加賜珍羞衣服。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming honored the aged; Xiang's mother was nearing eighty; together with Xiao Chen, Fu Zhao, and Lu Gao he each month regularly sent inquiries after her and added gifts of delicacies and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaoming honored the aged. Xiang's mother was nearly eighty, and together with Xiao Chen, Fu Zhao, and Lu Gao he sent monthly inquiries and gifts of delicacies and clothing.

sentences.zh: 襄母常卒患心痛，醫方須三升粟漿。

translations.literal: Xiang's mother often suddenly suffered heart pain; the medical prescription required three sheng of millet gruel.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's mother often suffered sudden heart pain, and the prescription called for three sheng of millet gruel.

sentences.zh: 時冬月，日又逼暮，求索無所，忽有老人詣門貨漿量如方劑。

translations.literal: It was winter, and the day was nearly dusk; they searched everywhere in vain; suddenly an old man came to the door selling gruel in the amount prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: It was winter and nearly dusk; they searched everywhere without success. Then an old man came to the door selling exactly the amount prescribed.

sentences.zh: 始欲酬直，無何失之，時以襄孝感所致。

translations.literal: They were just about to pay him when he vanished; people at the time attributed it to Xiang's filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: They were about to pay him when he vanished. People at the time attributed it to Xiang's filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 後為太子家令，復掌管記，母憂去職。

translations.literal: Later he became the Crown Prince's household steward, again managing the diary; on his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became the crown prince's household steward and again managed the diary, but left office when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 襄年已五十，毀頓過禮，太子憂之，日遣使誡喻。

translations.literal: Xiang was already fifty; his mourning debilitation exceeded ritual propriety; the Crown Prince worried and each day sent envoys to admonish and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was already fifty and mourned so severely that he exceeded ritual propriety. The crown prince worried and sent messengers every day to admonish him.

sentences.zh: 又有彭、李二家，先因忿爭，遂相誣告。

translations.literal: There were also the Peng and Li families, who first quarreled in anger and then accused each other falsely.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Peng and Li families, who had quarreled in anger and then brought false accusations against each other.

sentences.zh: 襄引入內室，不加責誚，但和言解喻之。

translations.literal: Xiang brought them into an inner room, did not rebuke them, but gently reasoned with them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang brought them into an inner room, did not rebuke them, and gently reasoned with them.

sentences.zh: 二人感恩，深自悔咎。

translations.literal: The two men were grateful and deeply repented.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were grateful and deeply repented.

sentences.zh: 乃為設酒食令其盡歡，酒罷同載而還，因相親厚。

translations.literal: He then set out wine and food for them to enjoy fully; when the wine was done they rode back in the same carriage and became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: He then set out wine and food for them to enjoy together; when the drinking was over they rode back in the same carriage and became close friends.

sentences.zh: 人又歌曰：「陸君政，無怨家。

translations.literal: People also sang: "Under Lord Lu's rule, no feuding families.
translations.idiomatic: People also sang: "Under Lord Lu's rule there are no feuding families.

sentences.zh: 鬥既罷，讎共車。

translations.literal: When the fight ends, enemies share a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the quarrel ends, enemies ride in the same carriage.

sentences.zh: 」在政六年，郡中大寧。

translations.literal: " He governed six years, and the commandery was greatly at peace.
translations.idiomatic: " He governed for six years, and the commandery was greatly at peace.

sentences.zh: 郡人李睍等四百二十人詣闕拜表，陳襄德化，求於郡立碑，降敕許之。

translations.literal: Four hundred twenty commandery people including Li Ming went to the capital to present a memorial praising Xiang's virtuous transformation and asking to erect a stele in the commandery; an edict was issued granting it.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred and twenty commandery residents, including Li Ming, went to court with a memorial praising Xiang's virtuous rule and asking that a stele be erected in the commandery; the throne granted it.

sentences.zh: 又表乞留襄，襄固乞還。

translations.literal: They also memorialized asking to retain Xiang; Xiang firmly asked to return.
translations.idiomatic: They also memorialized asking that Xiang be kept on, but Xiang firmly asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 襄弱冠遭家禍，釋服猶若居憂，終身蔬食布衣，不聽音樂，口不言殺害五十年。

translations.literal: Xiang at capping age suffered family disaster; after mourning ended he still lived as if in grief; all his life he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, would not listen to music, and for fifty years never spoke of killing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang suffered family disaster at capping age. After mourning ended he still lived as though in grief; all his life he ate plain food and wore coarse cloth, would not listen to music, and for fifty years never spoke of killing.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，元帝贈侍中，追封余干縣侯。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan posthumously made him Palace Attendant and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yugan County.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was suppressed, Emperor Yuan posthumously made him palace attendant and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yugan County.

sentences.zh: 陸雲公

translations.literal: Lu Yungong
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yungong

sentences.zh: 雲公字子龍，襄兄完子也。

translations.literal: Yungong, style name Zilong, was the son of Xiang's elder brother Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong, styled Zilong, was the son of Xiang's elder brother Wan.

sentences.zh: 完位甯遠長史、琅邪彭城二郡丞。

translations.literal: Wan held the posts of chief clerk of Ningyuan and magistrate of both Langya and Pengcheng commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wan served as chief clerk of Ningyuan and as magistrate of both Langya and Pengcheng commanderies.

sentences.zh: 雲公五歲誦論語、毛詩，九歲讀漢書，略能記憶。

translations.literal: At five Yungong recited the Analects and Mao's Odes; at nine he read the Book of Han and could largely remember it.
translations.idiomatic: At five Yungong could recite the Analects and Mao's Odes; at nine he read the Book of Han and could largely remember it.

sentences.zh: 從祖倕與沛國劉顯質問十事，雲公對無所失，顯歎異之。

translations.literal: His father's cousin Wei and Liu Xian of Pei attempted ten questions; Yungong answered without missing one; Xian marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Wei and Liu Xian of Pei tested him with ten questions; Yungong missed none, and Xian marveled at him.
