sentences.zh: 及長，好學，有才思，為平西湘東王繹行參軍。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning, had literary talent, and served as traveling aide to Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong, General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he loved learning, had literary talent, and served as traveling aide to Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong, general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 雲公先制太伯廟碑，吳興太守張纘罷郡經途，讀其文歎曰：「今之蔡伯喈也。

translations.literal: Yungong had first composed the Taibo Temple stele; Zhang Zuan, Administrator of Wuxing, passing by after leaving his commandery, read the text and sighed: "Today's Cai Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong had earlier composed the Taibo Temple stele. Zhang Zuan, administrator of Wuxing, read it while passing through after leaving office and sighed: "This is today's Cai Yong.

sentences.zh: 」纘至都掌選，言之武帝，召為尚書儀曹郎，入直壽光省，以本官知著作郎事。

translations.literal: " When Zuan reached the capital and managed selection, he told the Emperor, who summoned Yungong as Secretariat Protocol Officer, entered duty at the Shouguang Bureau, and in that original office also handled the Editorial Director's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " When Zhang reached the capital and took charge of appointments, he told the emperor, who summoned Yungong as secretariat protocol officer. Yungong entered duty at the Shouguang Bureau and concurrently handled the editorial director's affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書黃門郎，兼掌著作。

translations.literal: He was promoted through the ranks to Secretariat Yellow Gate Officer and concurrently managed editorial work.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to secretariat yellow gate officer and concurrently managed editorial work.

sentences.zh: 雲公善弈碁，嘗夜侍坐，武冠觸燭火。

translations.literal: Yungong was skilled at go; once at night attending while seated, his martial cap touched the candle flame.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong was skilled at go. Once, while attending the emperor at night, his martial cap touched the candle flame.

sentences.zh: 帝笑謂曰：「燭燒卿貂。

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "The candle scorches your marten.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said: "The candle is burning your marten fur.

sentences.zh: 」帝將用為侍中，故以此戲之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was about to appoint him Palace Attendant, so he joked thus.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was about to appoint him palace attendant, and so joked with him in this way.

sentences.zh: 時天泉池新制鯿魚舟，形闊而短，帝暇日常泛此舟，朝中唯引太常劉之遴、國子祭酒到溉、右衛朱異，雲公時年位尚輕亦預焉。

translations.literal: At the time a new bream-shaped boat had been made at the Tianquan Pool, broad and short in form; in leisure the Emperor often rode this boat; at court he invited only Director of Ceremonies Liu Zhilin, Director of the National University Dao Gai, and Right Guard Zhu Yi—Yungong, though young in years and rank, was also included.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a new bream-shaped boat, broad and short, had been built at Tianquan Pool, and in his leisure the emperor often sailed it. At court he invited only Director of Ceremonies Liu Zhilin, director of the National University Dao Gai, and Right Guard Zhu Yi; though still young in years and rank, Yungong was also included.

sentences.zh: 太清元年卒，張纘時為湘州，與雲公叔襄兄晏子書曰：「都信至，承賢兄子賢弟黃門殞逝，非唯貴門喪寶，實有識同悲。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Taiqing. Zhang Zuan was then in Xiangzhou and wrote to Yan, uncle of Yungong and elder brother of Xiang, saying: "Capital mail has arrived; I learn that your worthy elder brother's worthy younger brother, the Yellow Gate Officer, has died—not only has your noble house lost a treasure, but men of discernment mourn together.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Taiqing. Zhang Zuan was then in Xiangzhou and wrote to Lu Yan, Yungong's uncle and Xiang's elder brother, saying: "Mail from the capital has arrived. I learn that your worthy elder brother's worthy younger brother, the yellow gate officer, has died—not only has your noble house lost a treasure, but all who knew him mourn together.

sentences.zh: 」其為士流稱重如此。

translations.literal: " He was so esteemed among gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held among gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 雲公從父兄才子，亦有才名，位太子中庶子、廷尉，與雲公並有文集行於世。

translations.literal: Yungong's paternal cousin Caizi also had a literary reputation, held posts as Crown Prince's Household Steward and Commandant of Justice, and together with Yungong had collected writings circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong's paternal cousin Caizi also had a literary reputation. He served as crown prince's household steward and commandant of justice, and he and Yungong both had collected writings in circulation.

sentences.zh: 雲公子瓊字伯玉，幼聰慧，有思理。

translations.literal: Yungong's son Qiong, style name Boyu, was clever from youth and had thoughtful judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong's son Qiong, styled Boyu, was clever from childhood and had thoughtful judgment.

sentences.zh: 六歲為五言詩，頗有詞采。

translations.literal: At six he composed pentasyllabic verse with considerable literary grace.
translations.idiomatic: At six he wrote pentasyllabic poems with real literary grace.

sentences.zh: 大同末，雲公受梁武帝詔校定碁品，到溉、朱異以下並集。

translations.literal: Near the end of Datong, Yungong received Emperor Wu of Liang's edict to revise go rankings; Dao Gai, Zhu Yi, and others all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Datong, Yungong received an edict from Emperor Wu of Liang to revise go rankings, and Dao Gai, Zhu Yi, and others all gathered.

sentences.zh: 瓊時年八歲，於客前覆局，由是都下號曰神童。

translations.literal: Qiong was then eight; before the guests he reconstructed the board position, and thereafter the capital called him a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was then eight. Before the guests he reconstructed the whole board from memory, and thereafter the capital called him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 異言之武帝，召見，瓊風神警亮，進退詳審，帝甚異之。

translations.literal: Yi told the Emperor, who summoned him; Qiong's bearing was alert and bright, his comings and goings careful and measured; the Emperor marveled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi told the emperor, who summoned Qiong. His bearing was alert and bright, his manners careful and measured, and the emperor was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 十一，丁父憂，毀瘠有至性，從祖襄歎曰：「此兒必荷門基，所謂一不為少。

translations.literal: At eleven he entered mourning for his father; his emaciation from grief showed utmost sincerity; his father's cousin Xiang sighed: "This boy will surely sustain the house; as they say, one is not too few.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he entered mourning for his father and grew so emaciated with grief that his sincerity was unmistakable. His father's cousin Xiang sighed: "This boy will surely sustain the house—as they say, one is not too few.

sentences.zh: 」及侯景作逆，攜母避地於縣之西鄉，勤苦讀書，晝夜無怠，遂博學善屬文。

translations.literal: " When Hou Jing rebelled, he fled with his mother to the western district of the county, studied diligently day and night without slackening, and came to be broadly learned and skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: " When Hou Jing rebelled, he fled with his mother to the western district of the county, studied hard day and night without rest, and became broadly learned and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，以文學累遷尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: During the Tianjia era of Chen, through literary accomplishment he was promoted through the ranks to Secretariat Acting Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjia era of Chen he rose through literary talent to secretariat acting registrar.

sentences.zh: 瓊素有令名，深為陳文帝所賞。

translations.literal: Qiong had long had a fine reputation and was deeply appreciated by Emperor Wen of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong had long enjoyed a fine reputation and was deeply valued by Emperor Wen of Chen.

sentences.zh: 及討周迪、陳寶應等，都官符及諸大手筆，並中敕付瓊。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Zhou Di, Chen Baoying, and others, all the capital proclamations and major state documents were by imperial order entrusted to Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: When the court campaigned against Zhou Di, Chen Baoying, and others, all capital proclamations and major state documents were entrusted to Qiong by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 遷新安王文學，掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Literary Aide to the Prince of Xin'an and managed the Eastern Palace diary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to literary aide to the Prince of Xin'an and managed the eastern palace diary.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝為司徒，妙簡僚佐，吏部尚書徐陵薦瓊于宣帝，言瓊「識具優敏，文史足用，進居郎署，歲月過淹，左西掾缺，允膺茲選，雖階次小踰，其屈滯已積」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan became Minister of Works, he finely selected aides; Minister of Personnel Xu Ling recommended Qiong to Emperor Xuan, saying of Qiong: "His discernment is superior and quick, his learning in history and letters fully adequate; he entered the secretariat long ago and time has dragged on; the Left Western Aide post is vacant and he truly merits this selection; though his rank slightly overshoots precedent, his long stagnation has piled up."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan became minister of works and carefully selected aides, Minister of Personnel Xu Ling recommended Qiong to him, saying: "Qiong is quick and discerning, fully adequate in history and letters. He entered the secretariat long ago and has waited too long. The left western aide post is vacant and he truly deserves the appointment. Though his rank would be slightly above precedent, his long stagnation has already piled up."

sentences.zh: 乃除司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Left Western Aide of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed left western aide of the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 尋兼通直散騎常侍，聘齊。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as Regular Attendant of the General-in-chief of Expeditious Cavalry and went as envoy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served as regular attendant of the general-in-chief of expeditious cavalry and went as envoy to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 太建中為給事黃門侍郎，轉中庶子，領大著作，撰國史。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he was Supervising Secretary and Yellow Gate Officer, transferred to Household Steward, concurrently headed the Grand Editorial Office, and compiled the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he became supervising secretary and yellow gate officer, then household steward, concurrently headed the grand editorial office, and compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，直中書省，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord acceded, he entered duty at the Secretariat and managed edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When the later lord acceded, he entered duty at the secretariat and managed edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，除度支尚書，參選事，掌誥詔，並判廷尉、建康二獄事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed Minister of Revenue, participated in selection affairs, managed grand proclamations, and concurrently judged cases at the Commandant of Justice and the two prisons of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed minister of revenue, participated in selection affairs, managed grand proclamations, and concurrently judged cases for the commandant of justice and the two prisons of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 初，瓊父雲公奉梁武敕撰嘉瑞記，瓊述其旨而續焉，自永定訖於至德，勒成一家之言。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qiong's father Yungong had received Liang Wu's edict to compile a Record of Auspicious Omens; Qiong set forth its purpose and continued it, from Yongding through Zhide, completing a unified work.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qiong's father Yungong, by edict of Emperor Wu of Liang, had compiled a Record of Auspicious Omens. Qiong followed his intent and continued it from Yongding through Zhide, completing a unified work.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，著作如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel, his editorial duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of personnel while keeping his editorial duties.

sentences.zh: 瓊詳練譜牒，雅有識鑒。

translations.literal: Qiong was thoroughly versed in genealogical registers and had fine discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was thoroughly versed in genealogical registers and had excellent discernment.

sentences.zh: 先是吏部尚書宗元饒卒，尚書右僕射袁憲舉瓊，宣帝未之用，至是居之，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Earlier when Minister of Personnel Zong Yuanrao died, Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Xian recommended Qiong, but Emperor Xuan had not yet employed him; now that he held the post, he was called fully adequate to it.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Personnel Zong Yuanrao had earlier died, Vice Director Yuan Xian recommended Qiong, but Emperor Xuan had not yet appointed him. Now that he held the post, he was said to be fully adequate to it.

sentences.zh: 瓊性謙儉，不自封植，雖位望日隆，而執志逾下。

translations.literal: Qiong was by nature modest and frugal, not self-aggrandizing; though rank and repute rose daily, his resolve grew ever more humble.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was modest and frugal by nature and did not promote himself. Though rank and reputation rose daily, his resolve grew ever humbler.

sentences.zh: 園池室宇，無所改作，車馬衣服，不尚鮮華，四時祿俸，皆散之宗族，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Gardens, ponds, and dwellings he did not alter; carriages, horses, and clothes he did not favor for splendor; seasonal salary he distributed to the clan, and the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He altered none of his gardens, ponds, or dwellings; he did not favor splendid carriages, horses, or clothes; he gave his seasonal salary to the clan, and his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 暮年深懷止足，思避權要，恒謝疾不視事。

translations.literal: In his later years he deeply embraced knowing when to stop; wishing to avoid power and influence, he constantly pleaded illness and did not attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he deeply embraced knowing when to stop. Wishing to avoid power and influence, he constantly pleaded illness and declined to attend to business.

sentences.zh: 俄丁母憂。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 初瓊之侍東宮，母隨在官舍，及喪還鄉，詔加賻贈，後主自製志銘，朝野榮之。

translations.literal: When Qiong first served the Eastern Palace, his mother followed him to the official residence; when she died and he returned home, an edict added funeral gifts; the Later Lord himself composed the epitaph, and court and populace honored him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiong first served the eastern palace, his mother lived with him in the official residence. When she died and he returned home, the throne added funeral gifts; the later lord himself composed the epitaph, and court and country honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 瓊哀慕過毀，以至德四年卒。

translations.literal: Qiong's grief and longing exceeded propriety, and he died in the fourth year of Zhide.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong mourned so excessively that he died in the fourth year of Zhide.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: A collection in twenty fascicles circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection in twenty fascicles circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 陸從典

translations.literal: Lu Congdian
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congdian

sentences.zh: 子從典，字由儀，幼聰敏。

translations.literal: Congdian, style name Youyi, was clever from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Congdian, styled Youyi, was clever from childhood.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，讀沈約集，見回文研銘，援筆擬之，便有佳致。

translations.literal: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works, saw the palindrome inscription on the inkstone, took up the brush to imitate it, and at once achieved fine effect.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works, saw a palindrome inscription on an inkstone, took up the brush to imitate it, and at once produced a fine piece.

sentences.zh: 十二作柳賦，其詞甚美。

translations.literal: At twelve he composed a Willow Rhapsody; its wording was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he wrote a Willow Rhapsody of very fine wording.

sentences.zh: 從父瑜特所賞愛。

translations.literal: His father's cousin Yu especially prized and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Yu especially prized and loved him.

sentences.zh: 及瑜將終，命家中墳籍皆付之，從典乃集瑜文為十卷，仍制集序，其文甚工。

translations.literal: When Yu was near death, he ordered all the family's books and writings entrusted to him; Congdian then collected Yu's writings into ten fascicles and also composed a preface to the collection; the text was very skillful.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu was near death he entrusted all the family's books and writings to him. Congdian then collected Yu's writings into ten fascicles and also wrote a preface to the collection in very polished prose.

sentences.zh: 從典篤好學業，博涉群書，位太子洗馬、司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: Congdian devotedly loved scholarly work, read widely among books, and held the posts of Crown Prince's Groom and Left Western Aide of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Congdian devotedly loved scholarship, read widely, and served as crown prince's groom and left western aide of the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，位著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he entered Sui and held the post of Editorial Aide.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he entered Sui and served as editorial aide.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射楊素奏從典續司馬遷史記迄于隋，其書未就，坐弟受漢王諒職免。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Yang Su memorialized that Congdian continue Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian down to Sui; the book was not completed; he was dismissed because his younger brother accepted office under Prince of Han Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yang Su memorialized that Congdian continue Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian down to Sui. The book was not finished, and he was dismissed because his younger brother accepted office under Prince Liang of Han.

sentences.zh: 後卒於南陽縣主簿。

translations.literal: Later he died as chief secretary of Nanyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as chief secretary of Nanyang County.

sentences.zh: 琰字溫玉，瓊之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Wenyu, was Qiong's paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Wenyu, was Qiong's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 父令公，梁中軍宣城王記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Linggong was secretary to the Prince of Xuancheng, General of the Central Army, under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Linggong was secretary to the Prince of Xuancheng, general of the central army, under Liang.

sentences.zh: 琰幼孤，好學，有志操，州舉秀才。

translations.literal: Yan was orphaned in youth, loved learning, had firm character, and was nominated as a talent by the province.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was orphaned young, loved learning, had firm character, and was nominated as a provincial talent.

sentences.zh: 累遷宣惠始興王外兵參軍，直嘉德殿學士。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became External Military Aide to the Prince of Shixing, entitled Xuanhui, and Scholar on duty at the Jiade Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to external military aide to the Prince of Shixing, entitled Xuanhui, and scholar on duty at the Jiade Hall.

sentences.zh: 陳文帝聽覽餘暇，頗留心史籍，以琰博學，善占誦，引置左右。

translations.literal: In his spare moments from audience, Emperor Wen of Chen paid considerable attention to historical records; because Yan was broadly learned and skilled at recitation from memory, he was brought to attend at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare moments from governing, Emperor Wen of Chen took a keen interest in historical records. Finding Yan broadly learned and gifted at recitation from memory, he kept him close at hand.

sentences.zh: 嘗使制刀銘，琰援筆即成，無所點竄，帝嗟賞久之，賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had him compose an inscription for a knife; Yan took up the brush and finished at once without a single revision, and the emperor sighed in admiration for a long time and bestowed one suit of clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor asked him to compose an inscription for a knife. Yan took up the brush and finished at once without changing a word. The emperor admired him at length and gave him a suit of clothes.

sentences.zh: 俄兼通直散騎常侍，副琅邪王厚聘齊，至鄴而厚卒，琰為使主。

translations.literal: Before long he also served as Regular Attendant of the General-in-chief of Expeditious Cavalry and accompanied Hou, Prince of Langye, on a goodwill mission to Qi; when they reached Ye, Hou died, and Yan became chief envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served as regular attendant of the general-in-chief of expeditious cavalry and accompanied Hou, Prince of Langye, on a goodwill mission to Northern Qi. When they reached Ye, Hou died, and Yan became chief envoy.

sentences.zh: 時年二十餘，風氣韶亮，占對閑敏，齊士大夫甚傾心焉。

translations.literal: He was then just over twenty, graceful and bright in bearing, quick and apt in audience and reply, and the gentry of Qi were deeply drawn to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then just over twenty, graceful and bright in bearing, quick and polished in audience and reply, and the gentry of Qi were deeply drawn to him.

sentences.zh: 太建初，為武陵王明威府功曹史，兼東宮管記。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taijian era he served as Staff Officer in the household of the Prince of Wuling, entitled Mingwei, and concurrently as Eastern Palace diary keeper.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taijian era he served as staff officer in the household of the Prince of Wuling, entitled Mingwei, and concurrently as eastern palace diary keeper.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂去官，卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he resigned office and soon died.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，追贈司農卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 琰寡欲，鮮矜競，遊心經籍，晏如也。

translations.literal: Yan had few desires and little taste for rivalry; his heart rested in the classics, and he was perfectly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yan wanted little and contended little; his heart rested in the classics, and he was perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 所制文筆，多不存本，後主求其遺文，撰成二卷。

translations.literal: Most of the writings he composed did not survive in the original drafts; the later lord sought out his remaining texts and had them compiled into two scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the writings he composed did not survive in the original drafts. The later lord sought out his remaining texts and had them compiled into two scrolls.

sentences.zh: 弟瑜字幹玉，少篤學，美詞藻，州舉秀才。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yu, style name Ganyu, from youth devoted himself to learning, had fine literary talent, and was nominated as a provincial talent.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yu, styled Ganyu, devoted himself to learning from youth, had fine literary talent, and was nominated as a provincial talent.

sentences.zh: 再遷軍師晉安王外兵參軍，東宮學士。

translations.literal: After a second promotion he became External Military Aide to the Prince of Jin'an, Military Adviser, and Eastern Palace Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: After a second promotion he became external military aide to the Prince of Jin'an, military adviser, and eastern palace scholar.

sentences.zh: 兄琰時為管記，並以才學娛侍左右，時人比之二應。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yan was then diary keeper; both entertained the heir with their talent and learning, and people of the time compared them to the two Yings.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yan was then diary keeper. Both entertained the heir with their learning, and contemporaries compared them to the two Yings.

sentences.zh: 太建中，累遷太子洗馬，中舍人。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he was promoted in succession to Palace Groom of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he rose in succession to palace groom of the heir apparent and palace attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 瑜聰敏強記，常受莊、老于汝南周弘正，學成實論于僧滔法師，並通大旨。

translations.literal: Yu was quick-witted with a strong memory; he regularly studied Zhuangzi and Laozi under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan and studied the Treatise on the Completion of Truth under Master Sen Tao, mastering the main principles of both.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was quick-witted with a strong memory. He regularly studied Zhuangzi and Laozi under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan and the Treatise on the Completion of Truth under Master Sen Tao, mastering the main principles of both.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子好學，欲博覽群書，以子集繁多，命瑜抄撰，未就而卒。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince loved learning and wished to read widely among the books; because the collected writings were too numerous, he ordered Yu to copy and compile them, but before the work was finished Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crown prince loved learning and wished to read widely, but the collected writings were too numerous, so he ordered Yu to copy and compile them. The work was not finished before Yu died.

sentences.zh: 太子為之流涕，親制祭文，仍與詹事江總論述其美，詞甚傷切。

translations.literal: The crown prince wept for him, personally composed a sacrificial text, and together with Household Steward Jiang Zong discussed his virtues; the language was deeply mournful.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wept for him, personally composed a sacrificial text, and together with household steward Jiang Zong discussed his virtues in language deeply mournful.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，追贈光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously enfeoffed as director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected writings in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 瑜有從父兄玠，從父弟琛。

translations.literal: Yu had a paternal cousin Jie and a younger paternal cousin Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had a paternal cousin Jie and a younger paternal cousin Chen.

sentences.zh: 玠字潤玉，梁大匠卿晏子之子也。

translations.literal: Jie, style name Runyu, was the son of Yan, Director of Imperial Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, styled Runyu, was the son of Yan, director of imperial construction.

sentences.zh: 弘雅有識度，好學能屬文。

translations.literal: He was refined and had discernment, loved learning, and could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: He was refined and discerning, loved learning, and could compose prose.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，徵為管記，仍兼中舍人。

translations.literal: When the later lord was in the Eastern Palace, Jie was summoned as diary keeper and concurrently served as palace attendant of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the later lord was in the eastern palace, Jie was summoned as diary keeper and concurrently served as palace attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾失明。

translations.literal: Before long illness left him blind.
translations.idiomatic: Before long illness left him blind.

sentences.zh: 將還鄉里，太子解衣贈之，為之流涕。

translations.literal: When he was about to return home, the crown prince removed his own garment and gave it to him, weeping for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to return home, the crown prince removed his own garment and gave it to him, weeping as he did so.

sentences.zh: 太建八年卒，至德二年，追贈少府卿。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Taijian; in the second year of Zhide he was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Palace Revenues.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Taijian. In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously enfeoffed as director of the palace revenues.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected writings in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 琛字潔玉，宣毅臨川王長史丘公之子也。

translations.literal: Chen, style name Jieyu, was the son of Qiugong, Chief Clerk to the Prince of Linchuan, entitled Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, styled Jieyu, was the son of Qiugong, chief clerk to the Prince of Linchuan, entitled Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 少警俊，事後母以孝聞。

translations.literal: From youth he was sharp and talented and was known for filial devotion to his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was sharp and talented and was known for filial devotion to his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，為給事黃門侍郎、中書舍人，參掌機密。

translations.literal: When the later lord succeeded to the throne, Chen became Supervising Secretary and Yellow Gate Officer and Secretariat Drafter, participating in the management of confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the later lord succeeded to the throne, Chen became supervising secretary and yellow gate officer and secretariat drafter, participating in confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 琛性頗疏，坐漏泄禁中語，詔賜死。

translations.literal: Chen's character was rather careless; for leaking palace secrets he was ordered to death by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's character was rather careless. For leaking palace secrets he was sentenced to death by edict.

sentences.zh: 陸杲字明霞，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Gao, style name Mingxia, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gao, styled Mingxia, was from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖徽字休猷，宋補建康令，清平無私，為文帝所善。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui, style name Xiuyou, served in Song as Acting Magistrate of Jiankang, was upright and impartial, and was favored by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui, styled Xiuyou, served in Song as acting magistrate of Jiankang. Upright and impartial, he was favored by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十五年，除平越中郎將、廣州刺史，加督，清名亞王鎮之，為士庶所愛詠。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia he was appointed General of the Suppression of Yue and Governor of Guangzhou with supervisory powers; his clean reputation was second only to Wang Zhenzhi's, and gentry and commoners alike praised him in song.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia he was appointed general of the suppression of Yue and governor of Guangzhou with supervisory powers. His clean reputation was second only to Wang Zhenzhi's, and gentry and commoners alike praised him in song.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，為益州刺史，亦加督，恤隱有方，威惠兼著，寇盜靜息，人物殷阜，蜀土安之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he became Governor of Yizhou, also with supervisory powers; he cared for the distressed with method, authority and kindness were both manifest, bandits and robbers were stilled, people and goods flourished, and the land of Shu was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he became governor of Yizhou, also with supervisory powers. He cared for the distressed with method, authority and kindness were both manifest, bandits were stilled, people and goods flourished, and the land of Shu was at peace.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，身亡之日，家無餘財，文帝甚痛惜之，諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: He died in office; on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth. Emperor Wen deeply mourned him and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. On the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth. Emperor Wen deeply mourned him and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Jian.

sentences.zh: 父叡，揚州中從事。

translations.literal: His father Rui served as Assistant Director of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rui served as assistant director of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 杲少好學，工書畫，舅張融有高名，杲風韻舉止頗類，時稱曰。

translations.literal: Lu Gao loved learning from youth and was skilled at calligraphy and painting; his maternal uncle Zhang Rong had a lofty reputation, and Lu Gao's bearing and carriage were much alike; people at the time said,
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gao loved learning from youth and was skilled at calligraphy and painting. His maternal uncle Zhang Rong had a lofty reputation, and Lu Gao's bearing and carriage were much alike. People at the time said,

sentences.zh: 「無對日下，唯舅與甥」。

translations.literal: "Under the sun there is no peer—only uncle and nephew."
translations.idiomatic: "Under the sun there is no peer—only uncle and nephew."

sentences.zh: 為尚書殿中曹郎，拜日，八坐丞郎並到上省交禮，而杲至晚，不及時刻，坐免官。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Registrar in the Secretariat's Central Office; on the day of his appointment all the eight chief ministers and their assistant directors came to the upper secretariat to exchange courtesies, but Lu Gao arrived late and missed the appointed hour, and for this he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting registrar in the secretariat's central office. On the day of his appointment all the chief ministers and their assistant directors came to the upper secretariat to exchange courtesies, but Lu Gao arrived late and missed the appointed hour, and for this he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: Later he served as Aide to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as aide to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，為相國西曹掾。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he became Western Aide in the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was established, he became western aide in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 天監五年，位御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianjian he held the post of Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianjian he held the post of imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 性婞直，無所顧望。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and unyielding, and he looked to no one for favor.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was upright and unyielding, and he looked to no one for favor.

sentences.zh: 時山陰令虞肩在任贓汙數百萬，杲奏收劾之。

translations.literal: At that time the Magistrate of Shanyin, Yu Jian, while in office had embezzled several million; Lu Gao memorialized to have him arrested and impeached.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu Jian, magistrate of Shanyin, had embezzled several million while in office. Lu Gao memorialized to have him arrested and impeached.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人黃睦之以肩事托杲，杲不答。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Huang Muzhi asked Lu Gao to intervene in Jian's case, but Lu Gao did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Huang Muzhi asked Lu Gao to intervene in Jian's case, but Lu Gao did not reply.

sentences.zh: 梁武聞之以問杲，杲答曰：「有之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang heard of it he questioned Lu Gao, who answered: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang heard of it he questioned Lu Gao, who answered, "So it is.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「識睦之不？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Do you know Muzhi or not?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Do you know Muzhi or not?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「臣不識其人。

translations.literal: " He answered: "I do not know the man.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I do not know the man.

sentences.zh: 」時睦之在禦側，上指示曰：「此人是也。

translations.literal: " At that time Muzhi was at the emperor's side; the throne pointed and said: "This is the man.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Muzhi was at the emperor's side. The throne pointed and said, "This is the man.

sentences.zh: 」杲謂曰：「君小人，何敢以罪人屬南司。

translations.literal: " Lu Gao said to him: "You are a petty man—how dare you ask the Southern Office to take up a criminal case for you?
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Gao said to him, "You are a petty man—how dare you ask the censorate to take up a criminal case for you?

sentences.zh: 」睦之失色。

translations.literal: " Muzhi turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: " Muzhi turned pale.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍張稷是杲從舅，杲嘗以公事彈稷，稷因侍宴訴帝曰：「陸杲是臣親通，小事彈臣不貸。

translations.literal: General of the Garrison Zhang Ji was Lu Gao's maternal uncle; Lu Gao once impeached Ji on official business, and Ji, taking advantage of attending a banquet, complained to the emperor: "Lu Gao is my close relative by marriage, yet for a trifling matter he impeached me without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: General of the garrison Zhang Ji was Lu Gao's maternal uncle. Lu Gao once impeached Ji on official business, and Ji, while attending a banquet, complained to the emperor: "Lu Gao is my close relative by marriage, yet for a trifling matter he impeached me without mercy.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「杲職司其事，卿何得為嫌。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Lu Gao's duty is to handle such matters—how can you take offense?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Lu Gao's duty is to handle such matters—how can you take offense?

sentences.zh: 」杲在台，號不畏強禦。

translations.literal: " At the censorate Lu Gao was known as one who did not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: " At the censorate Lu Gao was known as one who did not fear the powerful.

sentences.zh: 為義興太守，在郡寬惠，為下所稱。

translations.literal: He served as Grand Administrator of Yixing; in the commandery he was generous and kind, and those below praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand administrator of Yixing. In the commandery he was generous and kind, and those below praised him.

sentences.zh: 曆左戶尚書，太常卿。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Minister of the Left Household and Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held the posts of minister of the left household and director of the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 出為臨川內史，將發，辭武帝，於坐通啟，求募部曲。

translations.literal: He went out as Interior Administrator of Linchuan; as he was about to depart he took leave of Emperor Wu and, while seated, submitted an open petition requesting permission to recruit personal retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as interior administrator of Linchuan. As he was about to depart he took leave of Emperor Wu and, while seated, submitted an open petition requesting permission to recruit personal retainers.

sentences.zh: 帝問何不付所由呈聞。

translations.literal: The emperor asked why he had not submitted it through the responsible office for formal review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why he had not submitted it through the responsible office for formal review.

sentences.zh: 杲答所由不為受。

translations.literal: Lu Gao answered that the responsible office would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gao answered that the responsible office would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 帝頗怪之，以其臨路不咎問。

translations.literal: The emperor was rather displeased, but because Lu Gao was already on the road he did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was rather displeased, but because Lu Gao was already on the road he did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 後入為金紫光祿大夫、特進。

translations.literal: Later he entered court again as Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon with Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to court as grand master with gold seal and purple ribbon with special advancement.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡質子。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhi.

sentences.zh: 杲素信佛法，持戒甚精，著沙門傳三十卷。

translations.literal: Lu Gao had long believed in Buddhism, kept the precepts with great strictness, and wrote Biographies of Monks in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gao had long believed in Buddhism, kept the precepts with great strictness, and wrote Biographies of Monks in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 弟煦，學涉有思理，位太子家令，撰晉書未就。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu was broadly learned and thoughtful, held the post of Household Steward to the Crown Prince, and wrote a History of Jin that was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xu was broadly learned and thoughtful, held the post of household steward to the crown prince, and wrote a History of Jin that was not completed.

sentences.zh: 又著陸史十五卷，陸氏驪泉志一卷，並行于時。

translations.literal: He also wrote History of the Lu in fifteen scrolls and Record of Lichuan in one scroll, both of which circulated at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote History of the Lu in fifteen scrolls and Record of Lichuan in one scroll, both of which circulated at the time.

sentences.zh: 子罩字洞元，少篤學，多所該覽，善屬文。

translations.literal: His son Zhao, style name Dongyuan, from youth devoted himself to learning, read widely in many fields, and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao, styled Dongyuan, devoted himself to learning from youth, read widely in many fields, and was skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 簡文居蕃，為記室參軍，撰帝集序。

translations.literal: When Jianwen held a princely fief, Zhao served as Recorder on his staff and wrote the preface to the prince's collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen held a princely fief, Zhao served as recorder on his staff and wrote the preface to the prince's collected writings.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太子中庶子，掌管記，禮遇甚厚。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Household Steward of the Heir Apparent and diary keeper, and was treated with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to household steward of the heir apparent and diary keeper, and was treated with great favor.

sentences.zh: 大同七年，以母老求去，公卿以下祖道於征虜亭，皇太子賜黃金五十斤，時人方之疏廣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong he asked to leave office because his mother was old; officials from the three highest ranks down saw him off at the Zhenglu Pavilion, and the crown prince bestowed fifty catties of gold; people of the time compared him to Shu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Datong he asked to leave office because his mother was old. Officials from the three highest ranks down saw him off at the Zhenglu Pavilion, and the crown prince bestowed fifty catties of gold. People of the time compared him to Shu Guang.

sentences.zh: 母終，後位終光祿卿。

translations.literal: After his mother died, he later held the post of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness until his end.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, he later held the post of grand master for splendid happiness until his end.

sentences.zh: 初，簡文在雍州，撰法寶聯璧，罩與群賢並抄掇區分者數歲。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jianwen was at Yongzhou, he compiled Linked Pearls of the Dharma Treasure; Zhao together with the assembled worthies copied, selected, and arranged the material for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jianwen was at Yongzhou, he compiled Linked Pearls of the Dharma Treasure. Zhao together with the assembled worthies copied, selected, and arranged the material for several years.

sentences.zh: 中大通六年而書成，命湘東王為序。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhongdatong the book was completed, and the throne ordered the Prince of Xiangdong to write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhongdatong the book was completed, and the throne ordered the Prince of Xiangdong to write the preface.

sentences.zh: 其作者有侍中國子祭酒南蘭陵蕭子顯等三十人，以比王象、劉邵之皇覽焉。

translations.literal: Its authors included Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial University Xiao Zixian of Nan Lanling and thirty others, and it was compared to the Imperial Overview of Wang Xiang and Liu Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Its authors included palace attendant and director of the imperial university Xiao Zixian of Nan Lanling and thirty others, and it was compared to the Imperial Overview of Wang Xiang and Liu Shao.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陸澄學稱博古，而用不合今。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Lu Cheng's learning was praised as ancient and broad, yet its application did not suit the present age.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment says: Lu Cheng's learning was praised as ancient and broad, yet its application did not suit the present age.

sentences.zh: 夫幹將見重于時，貴其所以立斷，于事未能周務，書廚得所譏矣。

translations.literal: When a Ganjiang sword is valued in its time, what is prized is its power to cut decisively; if in affairs it cannot handle every task thoroughly, the epithet "library cupboard" finds its target.
translations.idiomatic: When a Ganjiang sword is valued in its time, what is prized is its power to cut decisively; if in affairs it cannot handle every task thoroughly, the epithet "library cupboard" finds its target.

sentences.zh: 叔明持身有檢，殆為人望，雅道相傳，可謂載德者也。

translations.literal: Shuming kept himself in check and was nearly a man others looked up to; refined tradition passed down through him—one may call him a bearer of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming kept himself in check and was nearly a man others looked up to. Refined tradition passed down through him—one may call him a bearer of virtue.

sentences.zh: 杲諒直見稱，罩文以取達，亦足美乎。

translations.literal: Lu Gao was praised for honest uprightness; Zhao attained advancement through letters—are these also worthy of praise?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gao was praised for honest uprightness; Zhao attained advancement through letters—are these also worthy of praise?

sentences.zh: 舊陸徽著傳，事蹟蓋寡，今以附孫杲上云。

translations.literal: Formerly Lu Hui had a biography, but the record of his deeds is rather sparse; it is now appended above his grandson Lu Gao, thus.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Lu Hui had a biography, but the record of his deeds is rather sparse; it is now appended above his grandson Lu Gao, thus.
